Şık 2 {However}'daki 'no longer holds a thick coat' ile çelişir. Şık 3 nedeni tersine çevirir (kıl dikilir, yeni kıl büyümez). Şık 4 aradaki kas halkasını atlar (doğrudan soğuk değil).
Water sipped through the day keeps the joints cushioned and mobile.
PARA-SAGLIK-70-85-068
According to the paragraph, why does the face turn red when we blush?

Blushing is the one signal the body cannot easily [hide].
{Because} a rush of emotion widens the tiny vessels in the face, more blood flows just beneath the skin and colours it red.
{So} the harder a person tries to stop it (which only sharpens the feeling), the more the cheeks may [glow].

Because emotion widens the facial vessels, so more blood flows near the skin
Because trying to stop it always cools the face
Because the vessels in the face grow narrower
Because blood drains away from the skin

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — duygu yüz damarlarını genişletir, deri altına daha çok kan gelir, kızarır. TAKTİK: yön fiiline dikkat — 'widens' (genişletir) ile 'narrower' (daralır) zıttır. Şık 3 tam bu yön hatası. Şık 4 'more blood flows' ile çelişir (kan çekilmez, artar). Şık 2 {So}'daki 'harder to stop → more glow' mantığının tersi + 'always'.
Balanced meals of protein and grains keep energy stable for hours.
PARA-SAGLIK-70-85-069
According to the paragraph, what can set off a contagious yawn?

A yawn is strangely hard to keep to [oneself].
{Because} simply seeing or even reading about a yawn can set one off, the reflex seems tied to how we mirror others.
{However}, why it spreads so easily (which science still cannot fully explain) remains an open [question].

Seeing or even reading about a yawn
A full scientific explanation of the reflex
Keeping the yawn entirely to oneself
Refusing to mirror the people around us

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi tetikleyiciyi açıkça verir — bir esnemeyi görmek ya da okumak bile esnetir. TAKTİK: 'what can set off' sorusunda tetikleyici fiili ara (seeing/reading). Şık 2 {However}'daki 'science still cannot fully explain' ile çelişir. Şık 3 ilk cümledeki 'hard to keep to oneself' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'mirror others' fikrinin tersi.
Frequent exercise strengthens the heart and lowers disease risk.
PARA-SAGLIK-70-85-070
According to the paragraph, how can we keep our balance with our eyes shut?

Our sense of balance rests on fluid sealed inside the [ear].
{Because} tiny hairs feel this fluid shift as the head moves and report the tilt to the brain, we can stand upright even with our eyes shut.
{However}, when an infection disturbs the fluid (which normally settles at once), the whole world can seem to [spin].

Tiny hairs feel the ear fluid shift and report the tilt to the brain
The eyes track the tilt of the head for us
An infection disturbs the inner-ear fluid
The fluid stops moving inside the ear

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — kulaktaki sıvının kaymasını tüyler algılar ve eğimi beyne bildirir, bu yüzden gözler kapalıyken de dik durabiliriz. TAKTİK: soru 'eyes shut' diyor; cevap göze bağlı OLMAYAN sistem (iç kulak) olmalı. Şık 2 gözü işin içine katar — soruyla çelişir. Şık 3 {However}'daki arıza durumunu (spin) mekanizma sanar. Şık 4 'fluid shift' ile çelişir.
A steady supply of fresh vegetables keeps the immune system robust.
PARA-SAGLIK-70-85-071
According to the paragraph, what causes motion sickness?

Motion sickness springs from a quarrel between the [senses].
{Because} the inner ear feels the motion of a car while the eyes, fixed on a book, report stillness, the brain receives two clashing [messages].
{So} it reads the mismatch as a sign of poison (an ancient false alarm) and answers with nausea.

A clash between the inner ear feeling motion and the eyes reporting stillness
The eyes and inner ear both reporting the very same motion
An actual poison that the body has really detected
The brain failing to receive any signals at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi çatışmayı tanımlar — iç kulak hareketi hisseder, gözler (kitaba kilitli) durgunluk bildirir; beyin iki zıt mesaj alır. TAKTİK: 'quarrel/clash between senses' anahtar; cevap uyumsuzluk olmalı. Şık 2 tam tersi (aynı mesaj) — çatışma yok olurdu. Şık 3 parantezdeki 'false alarm' ifadesiyle çelişir (gerçek zehir değil). Şık 4 'receives two messages' ile çelişir.
Warm honey water can soothe a sore throat during a cold.
PARA-SAGLIK-70-85-072
According to the paragraph, how do emotional tears differ from ordinary ones?

Not every tear carries the same [message].
{Because} the eye makes one kind to wash out dust and another, richer in stress chemicals, when we weep, tears do more than one [job].
{However}, why only humans cry from emotion (which no other animal seems to do) is still debated.

They are richer in stress chemicals than the tears that wash out dust
They are made only to wash out dust
They carry exactly the same message as other tears
They are the kind that every animal readily produces

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi farkı verir — duygusal gözyaşı stres kimyasalları bakımından daha zengindir. TAKTİK: iki tür karşılaştırılıyor; soru 'emotional' olanı soruyor, o cümledeki ayırt edici özelliği (richer in stress chemicals) al. Şık 2 diğer türün (toz) işini yapıştırır. Şık 3 ilk cümledeki 'not every tear the same' ile çelişir. Şık 4 parantezdeki 'no other animal seems to do' ile çelişir.
A regular bedtime helps the body settle into deeper, restful sleep.
PARA-SAGLIK-70-85-073
According to the paragraph, why does cutting a nail cause no pain?

It feels odd that cutting a nail causes no [pain].
{Because} the visible nail is made of dead, hardened cells pushed out from a living root, only the base hidden beneath the skin can feel.
{So} the part we trim (which was alive only at its buried root) is really a shield of [dead] material.

Because the visible nail is made of dead, hardened cells
Because the living root sits above the skin
Because the whole nail is alive and sensitive
Because trimming heals the nail instantly

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — görünen tırnak ölü, sertleşmiş hücrelerden yapılıdır, bu yüzden acımaz. TAKTİK: 'no pain' sorusunda his taşımayan yapıyı ara (dead cells). Şık 2 'hidden beneath the skin' ile çelişir (kök derinin altında). Şık 3 'made of dead cells' ile doğrudan çelişir. Şık 4 metinde olmayan iddia.
Eating slowly gives the gut more time to absorb key nutrients.
PARA-SAGLIK-70-85-074
According to the paragraph, how does shivering warm the body?

Shivering is the body's own way of striking a [match].
{Because} rapid muscle tremors burn energy and throw off heat, they warm us when the cold bites.
{However}, this defense drains fuel fast (which the body cannot keep up forever), so long exposure eventually leaves a person dangerously [cold].

Rapid muscle tremors burn energy and throw off heat
It saves fuel so the body can last forever
It cools the body further when the cold bites
It draws heat inward from the cold air outside

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — hızlı kas titremeleri enerji yakar ve ısı açığa çıkarır. TAKTİK: 'how warm' sorusunda ısı üreten fiili ara (burn energy, throw off heat). Şık 2 {However}'daki 'drains fuel fast / cannot keep up forever' ile çelişir. Şık 3 yön hatası (ısıtır, soğutmaz). Şık 4 fizik-dışı iddia (dışarıdan ısı çekmez, içeride üretir).
A brisk swim works nearly every muscle without straining the joints.
PARA-SAGLIK-70-85-075
According to the paragraph, what triggers a sneeze?

A sneeze is a sudden storm meant to clear the [nose].
{Because} an irritant tickles the lining and sets off a violent burst of air, dust and germs are blown out at great speed.
{However}, trying to hold one in (which forces that pressure back inward) can in rare cases do real [harm].

An irritant tickling the lining of the nose
Holding the sneeze in to build up pressure
Dust being blown out at great speed
The pressure being forced back inward

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi tetikleyiciyi verir — bir tahriş edici burun zarını gıdıklar ve şiddetli hava patlamasını başlatır. TAKTİK: 'what triggers' sorusunda başlatıcı nedeni ara (irritant tickles), sonucu (dust blown out) değil. Şık 3 sonucu tetikleyici sanır. Şık 2 ve 4 {However}'daki 'hold in → harm' riskidir, hapşırığı başlatan değil.
Warm fluids can loosen a stubborn cough during the winter.

name: Hızlı Okuma YÖKDİL-Fen (70-85)
words: According to the paragraph, how do atmospheric gases keep the Earth warm?

The Earth stays warm enough for life because of gases in its [atmosphere].
{Because} these gases let sunlight pass in but trap much of the heat trying to escape, the surface holds warmth like a blanket.
{However}, when human activity thickens this layer (which has grown denser since industry began), more heat is trapped and the planet steadily [warms].

By letting sunlight in but trapping much of the escaping heat
By blocking sunlight from ever reaching the surface
By letting all of the heat escape freely into space
By thinning the atmospheric layer over time

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — gazlar güneş ışığını içeri alır ama kaçan ısının çoğunu tutar (battaniye etkisi). TAKTİK: 'let in but trap' iki yönlü ifadeyi olduğu gibi eşleştir; bir yönü çeviren şıkkı ele. Şık 2 'let sunlight pass in' ile çelişir (girişi engellemez). Şık 3 'trap...heat' ile çelişir (ısıyı salmaz, tutar). Şık 4 {However}'daki 'thickens/denser' yönünün tersi (incelmez, kalınlaşır).
Deep ocean trenches remain among the least explored places on Earth.
According to the paragraph, how do green plants make their own food?

Green plants feed themselves using little more than light, air, and [water].
{Because} chlorophyll captures the sun's energy and uses it to build sugar from carbon dioxide, plants turn sunshine into food.
{So} nearly every creature depends on this quiet process (which also releases the oxygen we breathe) at the base of the food [chain].

Chlorophyll captures sunlight and builds sugar from carbon dioxide
They absorb ready-made sugar directly from the soil
They release oxygen and take in sugar from the air
They depend on other creatures for all their energy

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi süreci verir — klorofil güneş enerjisini yakalar ve karbondioksitten şeker üretir. TAKTİK: 'how make food' sorusunda üretim fiilini ara (build sugar from CO2). Şık 2 metinde olmayan iddia (topraktan hazır şeker). Şık 3 yön karıştırma (bitki oksijeni SALAR, şekeri kendi YAPAR; havadan şeker almaz). Şık 4 'feed themselves' ifadesinin tersi. Parantez (which also releases oxygen) yan bilgidir.
Honeybees communicate the location of flowers through a precise waggle dance.
According to the paragraph, why does the Moon stay in orbit instead of falling to Earth?

The Moon does not simply fly off into space, nor does it fall straight to [Earth].
{Because} Earth's gravity pulls it inward while its own motion carries it sideways, the Moon is held in a steady [orbit].
{So} what looks like endless circling (which never quite ends) is really a fall that keeps missing the ground.

Gravity pulls it inward while its sideways motion carries it past Earth
Earth's gravity does not reach as far as the Moon
The Moon has no motion of its own at all
The Moon is slowly flying off into empty space

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi iki kuvvetin dengesini verir — yerçekimi içeri çeker, Ay'ın yana hareketi onu Dünya'nın yanından geçirir; sonuç yörünge. TAKTİK: 'why stay in orbit' sorusunda İKİ etkenin birlikte çalıştığını gör (pull + sideways motion); tek etkeni silen şıkları ele. Şık 2 yerçekimini yok sayar. Şık 3 yana hareketi yok sayar. Şık 4 ilk cümledeki 'does not fly off' olumsuzlamasının tersi.
Volcanic eruptions can spread fine ash across thousands of kilometres quickly.
According to the paragraph, what does the water cycle actually do?

The water that falls as rain today may have crossed an ocean [yesterday].
{Because} the sun's heat lifts water into the air as invisible vapour, which later cools and falls again, the same water is used over and over.
{However}, this endless cycle (which adds no new water to the planet) simply moves the supply we already [have].

It moves the same water around without adding any new water
It creates brand-new water for the planet each year
It removes water from the planet permanently
It lifts water up only, never letting it fall back

Doğru cevap 1: {However} cümlesi özü verir — döngü gezegene yeni su eklemez, var olanı dolaştırır. TAKTİK: parantez ve ana cümle aynı fikri söyler ('adds no new water' = 'moves the supply we already have'); bu olumsuzlama cevabı belirler. Şık 2 tam bu olumsuzlamanın tersi (yeni su üretir). Şık 3 'used over and over' ile çelişir (kalıcı kayıp yok). Şık 4 'cools and falls again' ile çelişir.
Copper conducts electricity far more efficiently than most other common metals.
According to the paragraph, where does the added heat go during melting or boiling?

Ice, water, and steam are the same substance wearing three different [faces].
{Because} adding heat loosens the bonds that hold the particles in place, a solid can melt and a liquid can boil away.
{However}, during the change itself (which holds the temperature steady for a while) the added heat goes into breaking bonds rather than raising the [temperature].

Into breaking the bonds between particles, not into raising the temperature
Into raising the temperature even more quickly than before
Into forming brand-new bonds between the particles
Into cooling the substance back into a solid

Doğru cevap 1: {However} cümlesi anahtarı verir — hâl değişimi sırasında ısı, sıcaklığı yükseltmek yerine bağları kırmaya gider. TAKTİK: 'rather than' kalıbında cevap ilk taraftadır (breaking bonds). Şık 2 tam 'rather than raising temperature' ifadesinin tersi. Şık 3 yön hatası (bağları kırar, kurmaz). Şık 4 'adding heat' bağlamının tersi (soğutma). Parantez (which holds the temperature steady) aynı fikri destekler.
Bats navigate darkness by sending out sound and listening for echoes.
According to the paragraph, why do metals carry electric current so easily?

Electricity flows easily through some materials and barely at all through [others].
{Because} metals are full of loose electrons free to drift, they carry current with ease, while rubber and glass keep their electrons [tight].
{So} a wire is wrapped in plastic (which blocks the flow) to guide the current safely and stop it leaking away.

Because they are full of loose electrons that are free to drift
Because they hold their electrons tightly in place
Because they are wrapped in plastic insulation
Because rubber and glass pass current straight through them

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — metallerde serbestçe dolaşabilen gevşek elektronlar vardır. TAKTİK: iki zıt madde grubu karşılaştırılıyor (metal ↔ kauçuk/cam); soru metali soruyorsa metalin özelliğini al. Şık 2 kauçuk/camın özelliğini (tight) metale yükler — özne karıştırma. Şık 3 yalıtımı iletkenlik nedeni sanır (tersine, akışı engeller). Şık 4 kauçuk/camın işini tersine çevirir.
Deserts can swing from scorching days to freezing nights within hours.
According to the paragraph, why does a compass needle point roughly north?

A compass needle always swings to point roughly [north].
{Because} the Earth itself acts like a giant magnet with poles near its top and bottom, the needle lines up with these invisible lines.
{However}, the magnetic pole (which slowly wanders year by year) does not sit exactly where the true North Pole [lies].

Because the Earth acts like a giant magnet and the needle lines up with it
Because the needle is drawn to the true North Pole exactly
Because the magnetic pole never moves at all
Because the needle makes its own magnetic field

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — Dünya dev bir mıknatıs gibi davranır, iğne onun görünmez çizgilerine hizalanır. TAKTİK: neden Dünya'nın alanıdır; iğnenin kendisi kaynak değil, hizalanandır. Şık 4 bu yönü ters çevirir (iğne alan üretmez). Şık 2 {However}'daki 'does not sit exactly where the true North Pole lies' ile çelişir ('exactly' tuzağı). Şık 3 parantezdeki 'slowly wanders' ile çelişir.
Coral reefs shelter a remarkable share of all ocean species.
According to the paragraph, why can sound not travel through space?

Sound cannot travel across the emptiness of [space].
{Because} it moves only by pushing through particles of air, water, or solid, a vacuum offers nothing for it to [carry].
{So} the loudest blast on a distant airless moon (which has no atmosphere) would reach a nearby astronaut in total silence.

Because it needs particles to push through, and a vacuum has none
Because space is simply too cold for sound to move
Because sound moves faster than it can ever be heard
Because explosions in space release no energy at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — ses ancak parçacıkları iterek yayılır, boşlukta itilecek parçacık yoktur. TAKTİK: 'why cannot travel' sorusunda eksik olan koşulu ara (no particles). Şık 2 metinde olmayan yanlış neden (soğuk). Şık 3 konu dışı hız iddiası. Şık 4 patlamanın enerjisiyle sesin yayılma ortamını karıştırır. Parantez (which has no atmosphere) aynı fikri örnekler.
Green plants release oxygen while building sugar from sunlight.
According to the paragraph, why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?

A straw in a glass of water looks strangely [bent] at the surface.
{Because} light changes speed as it passes from water into air, its path bends at the boundary between them.
{So} the eye, which assumes light always travels straight (a fair guess on dry land), is fooled into seeing a break that is not truly [there].

Because light changes speed and bends as it passes from water to air
Because the straw itself actually bends inside the water
Because light always travels in a perfectly straight line
Because water makes the straw physically break apart

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — ışık sudan havaya geçerken hız değiştirir ve sınırda kırılır. TAKTİK: görüntü yanılsaması; gerçek eğilme değil, ışığın yolunun kırılmasıdır. Şık 2 ve 4 pipeti gerçekten eğilmiş/kırılmış sanır ({So}'daki 'not truly there' ile çelişir). Şık 3 gözün YANLIŞ varsayımını (parantez: 'assumes...straight') doğru sanır.
Earthquakes strike most often along the edges of drifting crustal plates.
According to the paragraph, why can a heavy steel ship float while a small coin sinks?

A heavy steel ship floats while a small coin quietly [sinks].
{Because} floating depends not on weight alone but on how much water a shape pushes aside, a hollow hull can displace enough to stay [up].
{So} the same steel that sinks as a solid lump (which pushes aside very little) will float once beaten into a wide, hollow form.

Because floating depends on how much water the shape pushes aside, not weight alone
Because steel is actually lighter than the water around it
Because the coin pushes aside more water than the ship
Because a solid lump of steel is hollow on the inside

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi ilkeyi verir — yüzme ağırlığa değil, şeklin ittiği su miktarına bağlıdır. TAKTİK: 'not X but Y' kalıbında cevap Y'dir (displaced water). Şık 2 metnin ilkesiyle çelişir (çelik sudan ağırdır). Şık 3 yön hatası (gemi daha çok su iter, madeni para değil). Şık 4 'solid lump' ile 'hollow' çelişir. Parantez (which pushes aside very little) katı kütleyi açıklar.
Lightning heats the surrounding air to temperatures hotter than the Sun.
According to the paragraph, why would walking be impossible without friction?

Without friction, the simple act of walking would be [impossible].
{Because} the grip between shoe and ground pushes us forward with every step, a floor with no friction would leave us sliding helplessly in place.
{However}, the same force that helps us move (which also wears down moving parts) quietly steals energy as heat in every [machine].

Because the grip between shoe and ground is what pushes us forward
Because friction only ever wears down moving parts
Because friction steals energy as heat from machines
Because a slippery floor actually gives a firmer grip

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — ayakkabı ile zemin arasındaki tutunma bizi ileri iter; o olmadan kayarız. TAKTİK: soru sürtünmenin YARARINI soruyor; {Because}'daki olumlu işlevi seç, {However}'daki olumsuz yan etkiyi değil. Şık 2 ve 3 {However}'daki yıpratma/enerji kaybıdır — 'only' tuzağıyla asıl işlevi gölgeler. Şık 4 mantık tersi (kaygan zemin tutuş vermez).
Migrating birds often follow the stars and the planet's magnetic field.
According to the paragraph, what really happens to the matter when wood burns?

When wood burns, it does not truly vanish but changes into new [substances].
{Because} the bonds in the wood and oxygen break and reform as ash, smoke, and gas, the total matter is neither made nor [destroyed].
{So} the flame we see (which feels like pure loss) is really matter rearranged, with energy set free as heat and light.

It is rearranged into new substances, neither made nor destroyed
It vanishes completely into nothing at all
It is truly destroyed and lost within the flame
It stays exactly as wood beneath a layer of ash

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi korunum ilkesini verir — bağlar kırılıp kül/duman/gaz olarak yeniden kurulur; madde ne yaratılır ne yok edilir. TAKTİK: ilk cümledeki 'does not truly vanish' olumsuzlaması, 'yok olur' şıklarını çürütür. Şık 2 ve 3 tam bu olumsuzlanan 'vanish/destroyed' ifadeleridir. Şık 4 'changes into new substances' ile çelişir. Parantez (which feels like pure loss) yanılgıyı anar.
Spider silk is stronger by weight than many steel threads.
According to the paragraph, what happens to mountain rock over vast stretches of time?

Even the hardest mountain is slowly worn down over vast [time].
{Because} wind, water, and ice chip away at the rock grain by grain, today's peaks become tomorrow's sand and [soil].
{However}, the same forces that destroy also build, as crushed rock (which settles in layers under the sea) is pressed into new stone.

Wind, water, and ice wear it down into sand and soil
It grows harder and taller as the ages pass
It stays completely unchanged because it is so hard
It is worn down only by ice, never by wind or water

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi süreci verir — rüzgâr, su ve buz kayayı tane tane aşındırır; zirveler kum ve toprağa döner. TAKTİK: 'what happens over time' sorusunda aşınma fiillerini ara. Şık 2 yön hatası (aşınır, yükselmez). Şık 3 ilk cümledeki 'worn down' ile çelişir. Şık 4 üç etkenli listeyi ('wind, water, and ice') 'only ice' diye daraltır — 'only' tuzağı. Parantez (which settles in layers under the sea) yapım evresinin süsüdür.
The human heart pumps blood through thousands of kilometres of vessels.
According to the paragraph, why do useful traits spread through later generations?

Living things are not designed all at once but shaped slowly by [survival].
{Because} individuals with useful traits tend to live longer and leave more young, those traits spread through later [generations].
{However}, this shaping follows no plan or goal (which many people wrongly assume), only whatever happens to work in a given place.

Because individuals that have them live longer and leave more young
Because evolution follows a fixed plan toward a clear goal
Because animals choose which traits they want to pass on
Because useful traits appear equally in every place

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — yararlı özelliği olan bireyler daha uzun yaşayıp daha çok yavru bırakır, özellik böyle yayılır. TAKTİK: doğal seçilim 'amaç' değil, hayatta kalma/üreme farkıdır. Şık 2 {However}'daki 'no plan or goal' ile çelişir — parantez 'wrongly assume' tam bu tuzağı uyarır. Şık 3 'no plan' ile çelişir (seçim değil, kendiliğinden). Şık 4 'work in a given place' ifadesiyle çelişir ('equally' tuzağı).
Sound travels much faster through water than through ordinary air.
According to the paragraph, why can family features travel down the generations?

Inside almost every cell lies a coded [instruction] for building the whole body.
{Because} DNA is copied and passed from parent to child, family features can travel down the [generations].
{However}, each copy is not always perfect (a small error called a mutation), and such changes are the raw material of evolution.

Because DNA is copied and passed from parent to child
Because every copy of DNA is always perfect
Because mutations erase all family features
Because DNA is built completely fresh in each new child

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — DNA kopyalanıp ebeveynden çocuğa geçtiği için aile özellikleri aktarılır. TAKTİK: 'travel down generations' aktarım fiiline bağlı (copied and passed). Şık 2 {However}'daki 'not always perfect' ifadesinin tersi ('always' tuzağı). Şık 3 mutasyonu yanlış tanımlar (özelliği silmez, değiştirir). Şık 4 'passed from parent' ile çelişir (sıfırdan yapılmaz).
Glaciers carve deep valleys as they creep slowly down mountain slopes.
According to the paragraph, why can just a few atom types form so many different materials?

Everything around us, from air to iron, is built from tiny [atoms].
{Because} the way a handful of atom types join together decides what a substance becomes, the same few building blocks form endless [materials].
{So} water and rock share the very same kinds of atoms (arranged in quite different ways), yet could hardly seem more unlike.

Because the way the atoms join together decides what the substance becomes

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — klorofil kırmızı ve maviyi soğurur, yeşili geri yansıtır; gözümüz yansıyan yeşili görür. TAKTİK: 'not for the light it uses but the light it throws away' pivotu cevabı verir (yansıyan renk). Şık 2 tam tersi (yeşili soğurur) — kullanılan renk görülmez. Şık 3 ilk cümledeki 'sunlight is white' ile çelişir. Şık 4 rengin yansımadan değil üretimden geldiğini sanır.
Hibernating animals survive the long winter on their stored body fat.
According to the paragraph, why does coral bleach and starve when the water grows too warm?

A coral reef looks like bare stone but in fact teems with hidden [life].
{Because} tiny algae live inside the coral and feed it with sugar made from sunlight, the two survive together as close partners.
{However}, when the water grows too warm (which drives the algae out), the coral starves and bleaches to a ghostly [white].

Because the heat drives out the algae that had been feeding it
Because the algae feed the coral even more in warm water
Because coral is only bare stone with no living part
Because warm water gives the coral extra sugar to store

Doğru cevap 1: {However} cümlesi nedeni verir — aşırı sıcak, mercanı besleyen algleri kovar; mercan aç kalıp beyazlaşır. TAKTİK: iki ortağın bağını gör (alg besler → alg giderse aç kalır). Parantez 'which drives the algae out' cevabı taşır. Şık 2 yön hatası (sıcakta daha çok beslemez, algi kovar). Şık 3 ilk cümledeki 'teems with hidden life' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'starves' ile çelişir.
Comets grow a bright tail whenever they swing near the Sun.
According to the paragraph, why does a cactus have spines instead of broad leaves?

A desert plant must hoard every single drop of [water] it can find.
{Because} broad leaves would bleed precious moisture into the dry air, a cactus shrinks its leaves to thin spines and stores water in a swollen [stem].
{So} what looks like a bare, hostile shape (which wastes almost nothing) is really a quiet masterpiece of survival.

Because broad leaves would lose precious moisture to the dry air
Because spines gather far more water than broad leaves would
Because broad leaves store water better than a swollen stem
Because the cactus has no real need to save any water

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — geniş yapraklar nemi kuru havaya kaybederdi; kaktüs bu yüzden yaprağı dikene indirir. TAKTİK: 'why spines not leaves' sorusunda su kaybını önleme mantığını ara. Şık 2 dikenin işini çarpıtır (su toplamaz, kaybı azaltır). Şık 3 metnin 'stores water in a swollen stem' çözümüyle çelişir. Şık 4 ilk cümledeki 'must hoard every drop' ile çelişir. Parantez (which wastes almost nothing) cevabı destekler.
Moving a magnet past a coil pushes its electrons into current.
According to the paragraph, what makes the Sun shine?

The Sun has blazed for billions of years without burning out like an ordinary [fire].
{Because} deep in its core the crushing pressure fuses hydrogen into helium and unleashes vast energy, the Sun runs on a process no ordinary flame could [match].
{So} the light warming your face (which left the Sun about eight minutes ago) is born from atoms merging, not fuel burning.

Hydrogen fusing into helium in its core, releasing vast energy
Ordinary fuel simply burning away like a campfire
Atoms splitting themselves apart in its core
Sunlight merely reflecting off its bright surface

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — çekirdekte hidrojen helyuma kaynaşır (füzyon) ve büyük enerji açığa çıkar. TAKTİK: 'not fuel burning' ({So}) ve 'no ordinary flame could match' ipuçları 'yanma' şıkkını çürütür. Şık 2 tam bu çürütülen 'burning' fikridir. Şık 3 yön hatası (füzyon birleşmedir, bölünme=fisyon değil). Şık 4 Güneş'in kendi ışığını ürettiğiyle çelişir.
Snowflakes form six-sided crystals as water vapour freezes in clouds.
According to the paragraph, why can we not see a black hole directly?

A black hole is a place where gravity has grown far too strong to [escape].
{Because} so much matter is crushed into so small a space that not even light can pull away, the region turns utterly [dark].
{So} we cannot see one directly (which is exactly what gives it its name), only the wild swirl of matter falling in around it.

Because its gravity is so strong that not even light can escape it
Because it is simply too far away to reach with telescopes
Because it gives off a blinding white light of its own
Because light passes straight through it without stopping

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — çekim o kadar güçlü ki ışık bile kaçamaz, bölge kapkaranlık olur. TAKTİK: 'why not see' sorusunda ışığın kaçamamasını ara. Şık 2 metinde olmayan gerekçe (uzaklık değil). Şık 3 'utterly dark' ile çelişir (parlak ışık vermez). Şık 4 'not even light can pull away' ile çelişir (içinden geçmez, yutulur). Parantez (which gives it its name) süstür.
Penguins huddle tightly together to share warmth through bitter storms.
According to the paragraph, why does looking at a distant star mean looking into the past?

When we gaze up at a distant star, we are really peering into the [past].
{Because} its light takes many years to cross the vast gulf of space and reach us, we see the star only as it was long [ago].
{So} some of the points we admire tonight (which may have burned out centuries back) no longer even exist.

Because its light takes many years to cross space and reach us
Because the star itself moves backward through time
Because our eyes are simply too slow to see the present
Because the star's light actually reaches us instantly

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — yıldızın ışığı bize ulaşana dek yıllar geçer, onu geçmişteki hâliyle görürüz. TAKTİK: 'looking into the past' sorusunda ışığın yol süresini ara. Şık 4 tam bunun tersi (anında ulaşır). Şık 2 saçma (yıldız zamanda gerilemez). Şık 3 gözü suçlar (mekanizma ışık gecikmesidir). Parantez (which may have burned out) süstür.
Desert foxes shed body heat through their unusually large ears.
According to the paragraph, how does a generator make electricity?

A motor turns electricity into motion, but a generator does the exact [reverse].
{Because} moving a magnet past a coil of wire nudges its electrons into a current, spinning a magnet can make electricity from bare [movement].
{So} a bicycle light powered by pedalling (which needs no battery at all) runs on this simple trick of magnet and coil.

By moving a magnet past a coil, nudging its electrons into a current
By turning electricity into motion, just as a motor does
By storing chemical energy inside a sealed battery
By burning fuel to heat up a coil of wire

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — mıknatısı bobinin yanından geçirmek elektronları akıma iter (indüksiyon). TAKTİK: jeneratör motorun TERSİDİR ('does the exact reverse'); 'motor gibi' diyen şıkkı ele. Şık 2 tam bu çürütülen 'motor' işidir. Şık 3 pili karıştırır (parantez: 'needs no battery'). Şık 4 metinde olmayan mekanizma (yakıt/ısı değil, mıknatıs/bobin).
Ant colonies dig tunnels that keep their underground nests cool.
According to the paragraph, why does the Earth keep its atmosphere while the Moon does not?

The air we breathe does not simply drift off into [space].
{Because} the Earth's gravity holds the blanket of gas close to the surface, our atmosphere stays wrapped snugly around the planet.
{However}, a smaller world like the Moon (whose weak gravity cannot grip any gas) is left airless and [bare].

Because Earth's gravity holds the gas close, while the Moon's is too weak to grip it
Because the Moon's gravity is actually stronger than Earth's
Because the Earth has no gravity acting on the air at all
Because the Moon's air simply froze into solid ice

Doğru cevap 1: {Because}+{However} karşıtlığı cevabı verir — Dünya'nın çekimi gazı tutacak kadar güçlü, Ay'ınki tutamayacak kadar zayıf. TAKTİK: iki cismin çekim gücünü doğru eşleştir (Dünya güçlü ↔ Ay zayıf). Şık 2 bu gücü ters çevirir. Şık 3 'Earth's gravity holds' ile çelişir. Şık 4 metinde olmayan iddia (donma değil, çekim zayıflığı). Parantez (whose weak gravity...) cevabı taşır.
Solar panels turn plain daylight straight into a flow of electricity.
According to the paragraph, why is the sea salty when the rivers that feed it are fresh?

Rivers run with fresh water, and yet the sea they pour into is [salty].
{Because} flowing water dissolves tiny amounts of mineral salt from the rocks and carries it down to the ocean, the salt slowly gathers where the water [ends].
{So} as the rivers keep arriving and the sun lifts only pure water back as vapour (which leaves all the salt behind), the sea grows saltier still.

Because rivers dissolve salt from rocks and carry it to the ocean, where it gathers
Because the rivers themselves are far saltier than the sea
Because falling rain adds salt straight into the ocean
Because the sun sprinkles extra salt into the seawater

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi zinciri verir — nehirler kayadan çözdüğü az tuzu okyanusa taşır, tuz orada birikir. TAKTİK: nehir tazedir ama tuzu TAŞIR; buhar saf su götürüp tuzu bırakınca deniz tuzlanır (parantez cevabı destekler). Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'rivers run with fresh water' ile çelişir. Şık 3 ve 4 tuzun kaynağını yanlış yere (yağmur/güneş) yükler — özne karıştırma.
Pollinating insects carry pollen from bloom to bloom as they feed.
According to the paragraph, why is the far side of a mountain range often a desert?

One side of a mountain range may be lush and green while the other lies [barren].
{Because} air forced up the slope cools and drops most of its rain on the way up, little moisture is left by the time it crests the [peak].
{So} the far side sits in a 'rain shadow' (which starves it of water), where deserts often spread.

Because the air drops its rain climbing the near slope, leaving little for the far side
Because the far side actually gets much more rain than the near side
Because the mountains make fresh rain on their dry side
Because the air grows wetter and wetter as it crosses the peak

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — hava yamaçta yükselirken soğuyup yağmurunu bırakır, zirveyi aştığında nem kalmaz. TAKTİK: 'rain shadow' mantığı — yağış yakın yamaçta düşer, uzak taraf kurur. Şık 2 yön hatası (uzak taraf az yağış alır). Şık 4 'little moisture is left' ile çelişir (nem artmaz, azalır). Şık 3 saçma (kuru tarafta yağmur yapmaz). Parantez (which starves it of water) cevabı destekler.
A vacuum lets no sound pass, leaving deep space utterly silent.
According to the paragraph, how is rich soil formed?

Rich soil is never a given but the slow gift of ages of quiet [change].
{Because} weather crumbles bare rock into fine grains while dead plants and animals rot down into dark matter, the two slowly mix into fertile [earth].
{So} a single inch of good topsoil (which can take whole centuries to build) is far more precious than it looks.

Weathered rock grains mix together with rotted plants and animals
It appears quickly wherever bare rock is lying exposed
It is made purely of crumbled rock, with nothing living in it
It forms only from dead plants, without any rock at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi iki bileşeni verir — aşınan kaya taneleri ile çürüyen bitki/hayvan karışır. TAKTİK: toprak İKİ kaynaklıdır (kaya + canlı kalıntı); tek kaynağa indiren şıkları ele. Şık 3 (sadece kaya) ve şık 4 (sadece bitki) bu ortaklığı bozar. Şık 2 parantezdeki 'can take whole centuries' ile çelişir ('quickly' tuzağı).
A woodpecker's skull cushions its brain against powerful repeated blows.
According to the paragraph, why does a vacuum flask keep coffee hot for hours?

A good flask can keep coffee steaming hot for [hours].
{Because} heat escapes mainly by passing through matter, a layer of near-empty vacuum between the flask's two walls gives it almost nothing to cross.
{So} the trapped warmth cannot easily leak away (which is also why the same trick keeps cold drinks cold), and the coffee stays [hot].

Because the near-empty gap gives escaping heat almost no matter to pass through
Because the vacuum keeps adding fresh heat into the coffee
Because heat actually escapes fastest through empty space
Because the flask's walls are made of specially warmed metal

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi ilkeyi verir — ısı çoğunlukla maddeden geçerek kaçar; iki duvar arasındaki vakum geçecek madde bırakmaz. TAKTİK: 'why stays hot' sorusunda ısı kaçışını ENGELLEYEN şeyi ara (vakum = madde yok). Şık 3 tam tersi (boşlukta hızlı kaçmaz, kaçamaz). Şık 2 vakumu ısı kaynağı sanır (yalnızca yalıtır). Şık 4 metinde olmayan iddia. Parantez (which...keeps cold drinks cold) aynı ilkeyi örnekler.
Tree rings reveal how much a tree grew during each year.
According to the paragraph, how does a solar panel make electricity?

A solar panel can make power from nothing more than [sunlight].
{Because} certain materials release a flow of electrons whenever light strikes them, the panel turns plain daylight straight into [electricity].
{However}, it falls silent at night (when no light reaches its surface), so its energy must be stored up for the dark hours.

Certain materials in it release a flow of electrons when light strikes them
It burns sunlight like a fuel to make a lot of heat
It stores electrons that it draws in from the night air
It works best at night, in the deepest darkness

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — bazı maddeler ışık çarpınca elektron akışı salar; panel ışığı doğrudan elektriğe çevirir. TAKTİK: 'how make electricity' sorusunda ışık→elektron akışını ara. Şık 2 yanma sanır (ışık yakmaz, elektron koparır). Şık 3 metinde olmayan iddia (gece havasından elektron değil). Şık 4 {However}'daki 'falls silent at night' ile çelişir. Parantez (when no light reaches...) süstür.
Owls can rotate their heads remarkably far to spot prey.

name: Hızlı Okuma YÖKDİL-Sosyal (70-85)
words: PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-001
According to the paragraph, why does a sudden shortage push a price up?

The price of a thing rarely stands [still] for very long.
{Because} a good grows dearer when buyers are many but sellers few, and cheaper when the balance tips the other way, price follows the tug between supply and [demand].
{So} a sudden shortage (which leaves eager buyers competing for scarce goods) drives the price up until fewer can afford it.

Because eager buyers compete for the scarce goods
Because sellers suddenly outnumber the buyers
Because the good has become cheaper to make
Because demand falls sharply while supply rises

Doğru cevap 1: {So} cümlesi kıtlığın sonucunu verir — az mal için istekli alıcılar yarışınca fiyat yükselir. TAKTİK: arz-talepte fiyatı çeken tarafı bul (çok alıcı + az mal = yukarı). Parantez 'eager buyers competing for scarce goods' cevabı taşır. Şık 2 tam tersi (satıcı bolluğu fiyatı düşürür). Şık 3 maliyet konusu, kıtlık değil. Şık 4 yön hatası (talep düşmüyor, mal azalıyor).
Public libraries in many towns now lend musical instruments to curious members.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-002
According to the paragraph, why does printing too much money reduce its value?

When prices climb across the board, each coin in your pocket buys a little [less].
{Because} printing too much money spreads more cash across the very same pile of goods, the value of that money quietly [falls].
{However}, a little inflation (which nudges people to spend rather than hoard) is often thought healthier than none at all.

Because more cash ends up chasing the same amount of goods
Because there are suddenly far fewer coins in circulation
Because each coin comes to buy more than it did before
Because goods become far more plentiful than the money

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — aynı mal yığınına daha çok para dağılınca paranın değeri düşer. TAKTİK: enflasyonda 'çok para / aynı mal' dengesini izle. Şık 2 tam tersi (para artar, azalmaz). Şık 3 'buys less' ifadesinin tersi. Şık 4 yön hatası (mal değil, para artıyor). Parantez (which nudges people to spend) süstür.
Several European museums now offer free entry on the first Sunday monthly.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-003
According to the paragraph, why did the printing press help ideas spread?

Before the printing press, every single book had to be copied by [hand].
{Because} a machine could suddenly stamp out identical pages by the thousand, ideas spread faster and farther than ever [before].
{So} knowledge once locked away in a few monasteries (which jealously guarded their rare volumes) poured out to ordinary readers across Europe.

Because it could stamp out identical pages by the thousand
Because it made books rarer and much harder to find
Because monasteries began copying books faster by hand
Because fewer people were able to read the printed pages

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — makine binlerce özdeş sayfayı basabildiği için fikirler hızla yayıldı. TAKTİK: 'why spread' sorusunda üretim ölçeğini ara (by the thousand). Şık 2 tam tersi (kitap bollaştı, azalmadı). Şık 3 elle kopyalamayı hız kaynağı sanır (makine onun yerini aldı). Şık 4 'poured out to ordinary readers' ile çelişir. Parantez (which guarded their rare volumes) süstür.
Ancient Greek athletes trained for years to compete at the sacred games of Olympia.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-004
According to the paragraph, why did factories replace small workshops?

For most of history, goods were made slowly by hand in small [workshops].
{Because} steam-driven machines could labour tirelessly and turn out goods in vast numbers, factories soon replaced the craftsman's bench.
{However}, this leap in output (which crowded workers into grim, smoky cities) brought hardship as well as [wealth].

Because steam machines could work tirelessly and produce goods in vast numbers
Because workshops made goods faster than factories could
Because factories actually produced far fewer goods
Because the new machines needed no fuel or upkeep

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — buharlı makineler yorulmadan ve çok sayıda üretebildiği için fabrikalar atölyelerin yerini aldı. TAKTİK: 'why replace' sorusunda üstünlüğü (tireless + vast numbers) ara. Şık 2 yön hatası (atölye daha hızlı değil). Şık 3 'vast numbers' ile çelişir. Şık 4 metinde olmayan iddia (yakıt gerekmez). Parantez (which crowded workers...) süstür.
Traditional folk dances are still performed at village weddings across Anatolia.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-005
According to the paragraph, why did cities swell so quickly?

For thousands of years most people lived scattered across the open [countryside].
{Because} factories and offices drew huge crowds seeking work into a few dense centres, cities swelled at astonishing [speed].
{So} today more of humanity lives in towns than on the land (a balance that tipped only recently), reshaping how we live and move about.

Because factories and offices drew crowds who were seeking work
Because people mostly preferred the quiet of the countryside
Because farms suddenly needed far more workers than before
Because the growing cities offered no work at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — fabrika ve ofisler iş arayan kalabalıkları kentlere çekti. TAKTİK: 'why cities swell' sorusunda çekim nedenini (work) ara. Şık 2 kırsalı tercih etseler kent büyümezdi — çelişki. Şık 3 tam tersi (insanlar tarladan kente gitti). Şık 4 'seeking work → cities' mantığıyla çelişir. Parantez (a balance that tipped only recently) süstür.
Radio broadcasts once gathered whole families around a single evening program.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-006
According to the paragraph, why can a team produce far more by dividing the task?

A single worker making a whole pin from start to finish is oddly [slow].
{Because} splitting the task so that each person repeats one small step lets them grow fast and skilled at it, a team can produce far more than the same number working [alone].
{So} the modern factory (which breaks every job into tiny parts) owes its speed to this simple idea.

Because each person grows fast and skilled at one small repeated step
Because each worker makes an entire pin alone from start to finish
Because splitting the task quietly slows everyone down
Because far fewer workers are then needed for each pin

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi ilkeyi verir — iş bölününce herkes tek adımda hızlanır ve ustalaşır, toplam üretim artar. TAKTİK: işbölümünün faydası uzmanlaşma/hızdır. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'whole pin...oddly slow' ile çelişir. Şık 3 yön hatası (hızlandırır, yavaşlatmaz). Şık 4 metinde olmayan gerekçe (işçi sayısı değil). Parantez (which breaks every job...) süstür.
Medieval universities awarded degrees in law, medicine, and theology to students.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-007
According to the paragraph, why was direct barter slow and clumsy?

Long ago, people swapped goods directly, trading grain for [cloth].
{Because} such barter only works when each side happens to want exactly what the other offers, trade stayed slow and clumsy without a common [measure].
{So} money arose as a token everyone would accept (which no one actually needs to use), letting a farmer sell grain to one person and buy cloth from another.

Because it only works when each side wants what the other offers
Because money had already made trading much harder
Because everyone happily accepted the very same token
Because grain simply could not be traded at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi zorluğu verir — takas ancak iki taraf da diğerinin sunduğunu istediğinde işler. TAKTİK: 'why clumsy' sorusunda karşılıklı istek koşulunu ara. Şık 2 zaman hatası (para SONRA çıktı, sorunu çözdü). Şık 3 parayı tarif eder, takası değil. Şık 4 'trading grain for cloth' ile çelişir. Parantez (which no one actually needs to use) süstür.
National anthems often borrow melodies from much older village songs.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-008
According to the paragraph, why must rulers in a democracy answer to the people?

In a democracy, power is meant to rest with the [people].
{Because} citizens choose their leaders by vote and can turn them out again at the next election, rulers must answer to those they [govern].
{However}, a vote alone is not enough (without free speech and fair courts), or the choice soon becomes hollow.

Because citizens can turn them out again at the next election
Because rulers simply choose themselves for life
Because the people have no real say in who governs
Because votes are counted only once a century

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi hesap verebilirliğin nedenini verir — halk seçimle yöneticiyi görevden alabildiği için yönetici halka karşı sorumludur. TAKTİK: 'why answer to people' sorusunda seçmenin gücünü (turn them out) ara. Şık 2 seçim mantığıyla çelişir (kendini seçmez). Şık 3 'power rests with the people' ile çelişir. Şık 4 metinde olmayan aşırı iddia. Parantez (without free speech...) süstür.
Handwritten letters between soldiers and their families fill many war archives.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-009
According to the paragraph, how did silk reach Rome all the way from China?

Long before ships crossed the open oceans, goods travelled overland between [East] and West.
{Because} traders passed silk, spices, and ideas from hand to hand along a long chain of routes, distant cultures touched without ever truly meeting.
{So} a Roman might wear Chinese silk (which had changed hands a dozen times) without ever knowing where it truly [began].

It was passed from trader to trader along a chain of routes
Roman traders sailed directly to China to fetch it
A single merchant carried it the whole way himself
The Chinese delivered it straight into Roman hands

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi yöntemi verir — ipek elden ele, uzun bir rota zinciri boyunca aktarıldı. TAKTİK: 'how reach' sorusunda aktarım biçimini (hand to hand / chain) ara. Şık 2 'before ships crossed oceans' ile çelişir (doğrudan deniz yolu yok). Şık 3 parantezdeki 'changed hands a dozen times' ile çelişir (tek tüccar değil). Şık 4 'without ever meeting' ile çelişir.
Modern census forms ask about age, occupation, and household size.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-010
According to the paragraph, what was the very first writing mostly used for?

Before writing, everything a people knew had to be held in living [memory].
{Because} marks pressed into wet clay could store a promise or a count long after the speaker had fallen silent, records began to outlast the [mind].
{So} the first writing was not poetry but plain accounts of grain and cattle (which someone badly needed to track), the dull roots of all literature.

Plain accounts of grain and cattle
Grand poetry and sweeping heroic stories
Long letters between distant friends
Recording living memory word for word

Doğru cevap 1: {So} cümlesi ilk yazının işlevini verir — şiir değil, tahıl ve sığır kayıtları. TAKTİK: 'not X but Y' kalıbında cevap Y'dir (accounts of grain and cattle). Şık 2 tam 'not poetry' ile çelişen çürütülen fikirdir. Şık 3 metinde olmayan kullanım. Şık 4 yazının bellek YERİNE geçtiği fikriyle çelişir (belleği kelimesi kelimesine kaydetmek değil). Parantez (which someone needed to track) cevabı destekler.
Olive oil remained a prized trade good around the ancient Mediterranean.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-011
According to the paragraph, why do families leave all they know behind to migrate?

People have always moved in search of a better [life].
{Because} war, hunger, or the simple hope of work drives families to leave behind all they know, migration has shaped every nation on Earth.
{However}, the newcomers are often met with suspicion at first (which time and familiarity tend to soften), even in places where they are sorely [needed].

Because of war, hunger, or the hope of finding work
Because they are always welcomed warmly wherever they go
Because migration has in truth shaped no nation at all
Because they are never truly needed anywhere

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi itici/çekici nedenleri verir — savaş, açlık ya da iş umudu aileleri göçe sürükler. TAKTİK: 'why migrate' sorusunda sürükleyen etkenleri ara. Because childhood was in truth better spent at the machine

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi gerekçeyi verir — makinede geçen çocukluk hem sağlığı hem eğitimi elden alır. TAKTİK: 'why bar children' sorusunda reformcunun ahlaki savını ara. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'tiny wages' ile çelişir. Şık 3 {However}'daki DİRENÇÇİLERİN iddiasıdır, reformcunun değil — taraf karıştırma. Şık 4 'robbed...of health and schooling' ile çelişir.
Village bakeries once shared a single communal oven among households.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-057
According to the paragraph, on what grounds did women demand the vote?

For most of history, the vote was a right jealously reserved for [men].
{Because} women argued that those who obey the laws and pay the taxes surely deserve a say in making them, movements rose up to demand the [ballot].
{So} a right once thought unthinkable (which many had solemnly sworn would ruin society) became, within a single lifetime, simply normal.

That those who obey the laws and pay the taxes deserve a say in making them
That the vote should stay firmly reserved for men alone
That allowing women to vote would surely ruin society
That women ought not to pay any taxes at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi savı verir — yasalara uyan ve vergi ödeyen, onların yapımında söz hakkını hak eder. TAKTİK: 'on what grounds' sorusunda talebin dayanağını ara. Şık 2 hakkın erkeğe saklı eski durumudur — talep bunun tersi. Şık 3 parantezdeki karşıtların ('would ruin society') sözüdür, kadınların savı değil. Şık 4 'pay the taxes' savıyla çelişir.
Mountain passes determined which valleys traded goods with each other.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-058
According to the paragraph, why is a pasture shared by all often stripped bare?

When a pasture belongs to everyone, it can end up truly cared for by [no one].
{Because} each herder gains fully by adding one more animal but shares the cost of the overgrazed land with all the rest, the common field is soon stripped [bare].
{So} a resource that no single owner protects (which all are free to use as they wish) is often the very first to be ruined.

Because each herder gains from adding an animal but shares the cost of overgrazing with all
Because a single careful owner closely protects it
Because the herders in fact add no animals at all
Because the whole cost falls on just one herder

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi 'ortak mera trajedisini' verir — fayda tümüyle çobanın, maliyet herkese bölünür; bu yüzden mera tükenir. TAKTİK: kötüye kullanım, kişisel kazanç ile paylaşılan maliyet dengesizliğinden doğar. Şık 2 'cared for by no one' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'adding one more animal' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'shares the cost with all' ile çelişir (maliyet dağılır). Parantez (which all are free to use) süstür.
Sailing clubs taught generations of coastal children practical seamanship skills.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-059
According to the paragraph, how does a refugee differ from a migrant?

Not everyone who crosses a border leaves home by free [choice].
{Because} a refugee flees war or persecution that makes staying deadly, while a migrant moves mainly in search of a better wage, the law treats the two quite [differently].
{However}, the line between them can blur (when hunger itself becomes a threat to life), and real people rarely fit into neat boxes.

A refugee flees deadly war or persecution, while a migrant moves for a better wage
A refugee moves for a better wage, while a migrant flees war
Both of them leave home purely by their own free choice
The law in fact treats the two groups exactly the same

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi ikisini karşıtlar — mülteci ölümcül savaş/zulümden kaçar, göçmen daha iyi ücret için taşınır. TAKTİK: iki tanımı doğru eşleştir; çaprazlayan şıkkı ele. Şık 2 tam bu çaprazlamadır. Şık 3 ilk cümledeki 'not...by free choice' (mülteci için) ile çelişir. Şık 4 'treats the two quite differently' ile çelişir. Parantez (when hunger becomes a threat) süstür.
Antique dealers travel widely searching for rare furniture and paintings.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-060
According to the paragraph, what does a bank do with most of the money savers deposit?

A bank does not simply lock your money away in a [vault].
{Because} it lends out most of what savers deposit and keeps only a fraction on hand, a bank turns idle savings into loans that build [businesses].
{However}, this whole arrangement rests on trust (which can vanish in a sudden panic), for no bank could ever repay every saver at once.

It lends most of it out as loans that build businesses
It locks every bit of it away safely in a vault
It repays every single saver at once on demand
It keeps the full amount permanently on hand

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi işleyişi verir — banka mevduatın çoğunu kredi olarak verir, elinde sadece küçük bir kısmı tutar. TAKTİK: bankanın özü 'atıl parayı krediye çevirmek'tir. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'does not simply lock away' ile çelişir. Şık 3 {However}'daki 'no bank could repay every saver at once' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'keeps only a fraction' ile çelişir. Parantez (which can vanish in a panic) süstür.
Summer schools help rural pupils keep pace with city classmates.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-061
According to the paragraph, how does insurance soften the blow of a disaster?

A single fire can ruin one family, yet barely dent a whole [town].
{Because} insurance gathers small payments from the many who stay safe to cover the few who suffer a loss, the blow to one is spread thin across [all].
{So} a person pays a little every year (which they quietly hope to waste) to be spared a disaster they could never face alone.

By gathering small payments from the many to cover the few who suffer loss
By making one unlucky family bear the whole loss alone
By paying nothing at all to those who suffer a loss
By collecting money only from the few who are harmed

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — sigorta güvende kalan çoğunluktan küçük ödemeler toplayıp zarar gören azınlığı karşılar; darbe herkese yayılır. TAKTİK: sigorta = riski havuzlama. Şık 2 'spread thin across all' ile çelişir (yalnız bırakmaz). Şık 3 'cover the few who suffer' ile çelişir. Şık 4 yön hatası (ödemeyi zarar görenden değil, güvendekilerden toplar). Parantez (which they hope to waste) süstür.
Cathedral construction sometimes stretched across three or four whole centuries.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-062
According to the paragraph, how did newspapers bring distant events into ordinary lives?

Before newspapers, most people knew only what had happened within a single day's [walk].
{Because} a printed sheet could carry the very same report to thousands of readers all at once, distant events entered the daily talk of ordinary [lives].
{However}, the same paper that informs a public (which cannot check every claim for itself) can just as easily mislead it with a single well-placed lie.

By carrying the same report to thousands of readers all at once
By limiting the news to events within a day's walk
By keeping printed reports from ever reaching readers
By carefully checking every claim before it was printed

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — basılı sayfa aynı haberi bir anda binlerce okura ulaştırır, uzak olaylar günlük konuşmaya girer. TAKTİK: 'how bring distant events' sorusunda kitlesel ulaşımı ara. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki eski, dar durumdur (gazetenin aştığı sınır). Şık 3 'carry to thousands' ile çelişir. Şık 4 {However}'daki 'cannot check every claim' ile çelişir.
Terraced fields let mountain farmers grow rice on steep hillsides.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-063
According to the paragraph, why did distance itself seem to shrink with the coming of the railway?

Before the railway, a journey of a hundred miles could swallow many weary [days].
{Because} a train could haul both people and goods overland at a speed no horse could ever match, distance itself seemed to [shrink].
{So} towns once cut off from the wider world (which the new tracks suddenly linked) were pulled into a single national market.

Because a train could haul people and goods at a speed no horse could match
Because journeys somehow took even longer than they had before
Because the towns simply stayed cut off from the world
Because the trains actually moved more slowly than horses

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — tren, insan ve malı hiçbir atın erişemeyeceği hızla taşıdı; mesafe küçülmüş gibi oldu. TAKTİK: 'why distance shrink' sorusunda hız üstünlüğünü ara. Şık 2 'swallow many days → shrink' mantığının tersi. Şık 4 'no horse could match' ile çelişir (yön hatası). Şık 3 {So}'daki 'towns...suddenly linked' ile çelişir. Parantez (which the tracks linked) süstür.
Pottery cooperatives give rural women a steady independent income today.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-064
According to the paragraph, why can an investor back a risky scheme without fear of losing everything?

Great ventures often carry risks far too heavy for one person alone to [bear].
{Because} a company can be treated in law as a separate person of its own, its owners risk only the money they actually put in and no [more].
{So} an investor can back a bold scheme (which might still fail outright) without any fear of losing his own house should it collapse.

Because the owners risk only the money they put in, and no more
Because the company itself can simply never fail
Because the owners must repay all of the company's debts
Because the investor alone bears the whole of the risk

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi sınırlı sorumluluğu verir — şirket ayrı bir tüzel kişi sayıldığından sahipler yalnızca koydukları parayı riske atar. TAKTİK: 'without fear of losing everything' sorusunda kaybın sınırını ara. Şık 2 parantezdeki 'which might still fail' ile çelişir (batabilir). Şık 3 'risk only...no more' ile çelişir (tüm borçtan değil). Şık 4 'too heavy for one person' ile çelişir. Parantez (which might still fail) süstür.
Pilgrimage routes supported inns, guides, and souvenir sellers along the way.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-065
According to the paragraph, why are distant economies woven ever more tightly together?

Today a single phone may be designed in one land, built in another, and sold in a [third].
{Because} cheap shipping and instant communication let firms spread their work right across the globe, distant economies are woven ever more tightly [together].
{However}, this deep connection (which has lifted millions out of poverty) also means that a shock in one place can ripple out to all.

Because cheap shipping and instant communication let firms spread work across the globe
Because each economy now works entirely on its own
Because a sudden shock in one place never spreads at all
Because firms keep all of their work within a single land

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — ucuz nakliye ve anlık iletişim, firmaların işi dünyaya yaymasını sağlar; ekonomiler böyle iç içe geçer. TAKTİK: küreselleşmenin motoru ulaşım+iletişimdir. Şık 2 'woven together' ile çelişir (yalnız çalışmaz). Şık 3 {However}'daki 'shock...can ripple to all' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'spread work across the globe' ile çelişir. Parantez (which lifted millions...) süstür.
Amateur theatre groups keep small community halls busy every winter.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-066
According to the paragraph, why does a museum help a society keep a shared thread of memory?

A museum gathers under one roof what time would otherwise quietly [scatter].
{Because} objects saved from many different ages let a visitor stand face to face with the distant past, a society keeps a shared thread of [memory].
{However}, what a museum chooses to display (which quietly shapes the story it ends up telling) can honour some voices while silencing others.

Because objects saved from many ages let visitors stand face to face with the past
Because it scatters its objects across many distant places
Because it displays every single object exactly equally
Because it tells no story about the past at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — farklı çağlardan saklanan nesneler ziyaretçiyi geçmişle yüz yüze getirir, ortak bellek korunur. TAKTİK: 'why shared memory' sorusunda nesnelerin geçmişi taşımasını ara. Şık 2 'gathers...what time would scatter' ile çelişir (dağıtmaz, toplar). Şık 3 {However}'daki seçici sergileme ile çelişir ('equally' tuzağı). Şık 4 'shapes the story it tells' ile çelişir. Parantez (which shapes the story...) süstür.
Grape harvests still bring whole villages into the fields each autumn.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-067
According to the paragraph, why did the clock come to rule the working day?

Before the factory, people worked by the loose rhythm of the sun and the turning [seasons].
{Because} a machine runs to a fixed schedule that pays no heed at all to daylight, the clock slowly came to rule the working [day].
{So} a whistle marking the start of a shift (which the sun had once only loosely set) taught whole populations to live by the hour.

Because a machine runs to a fixed schedule that pays no heed to daylight
Because the early factories worked by the rhythm of the sun
Because the sun itself set a precise working schedule
Because clocks paid the closest heed to the daylight

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — makine, gün ışığını umursamayan sabit bir çizelgeye göre çalışır, bu yüzden saat günü yönetir hâle geldi. TAKTİK: 'why clock rules' sorusunda makinenin sabit çizelgesini ara. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki eski, güneşe bağlı düzendir (saatin aştığı). Şık 3 'sun...only loosely set' ile çelişir (kesin değil). Şık 4 'pays no heed to daylight' ile çelişir. Parantez (which the sun once loosely set) süstür.
Carrier pigeons delivered urgent messages for banks and newspapers alike.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-068
According to the paragraph, how does diplomacy let states settle disputes without bloodshed?

When two states quarrel, the only choice need not be [war].
{Because} envoys can meet to trade concessions and find a bargain that both sides can just bear, diplomacy offers a way to settle disputes without [blood].
{However}, such talks work only while each side still fears the cost of fighting (which is what keeps them at the table), for words alone rarely bind the truly desperate.

Envoys meet to trade concessions and find a bargain both sides can bear
By forcing one side to surrender completely at once
By removing every last fear of the cost of a war
By refusing to meet or to bargain at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mekanizmayı verir — elçiler karşılıklı ödün verip iki tarafın da katlanabileceği bir uzlaşma bulur. TAKTİK: 'how without blood' sorusunda pazarlık/ödün fikrini ara. Şık 2 'both can bear' uzlaşmasıyla çelişir (teslim değil). Şık 3 {However}'daki 'each side still fears the cost' ile çelişir (korku masada tutar). Şık 4 'envoys can meet' ile çelişir. Parantez (which keeps them at the table) süstür.
Traditional wrestling festivals in Anatolia date back several proud centuries.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-069
According to the paragraph, why is a case put before a jury rather than a judge alone?

In some courts, a person's fate rests not with a single judge but with ordinary [citizens].
{Because} a jury drawn from the community judges the facts as reasonable people would, power over guilt is kept out of any one official's [hands].
{However}, twelve strangers can also carry their own quiet prejudices (which a fair trial must always work to hold in check).

So that power over guilt is kept out of any single official's hands
So that one single official decides every case alone
So that the wider community is given no say at all
So that personal prejudices alone decide the verdict

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi gerekçeyi verir — topluluktan seçilen jüri olguları değerlendirir; suç kararı tek bir görevlinin elinde toplanmaz. TAKTİK: 'why jury not judge' sorusunda gücün dağıtılmasını ara. Şık 2 tam tersi (tek görevli). Şık 3 'drawn from the community' ile çelişir. Şık 4 {However}'daki 'must hold prejudices in check' ile çelişir (önyargı karar vermemeli). Parantez (which a fair trial must check) süstür.
Street food vendors feed millions of busy commuters every morning.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-070
According to the paragraph, how does a patent reward the effort of creation?

An inventor who shares a bold new idea risks seeing rivals simply [copy] it.
{Because} a patent grants its holder a limited spell of sole right to profit from an invention, it rewards the hard effort of [creation].
{However}, the very same monopoly that spurs invention (which others may not use for years) can also hold back those who would build upon it.

By granting the holder a limited spell of sole right to profit from the invention
By letting rival firms copy the idea straight away
By giving the inventor no real rights at all
By sharing the profit equally with every rival

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi ödülü verir — patent, sahibine sınırlı süreli tekel kâr hakkı tanır, böylece yaratım emeği ödüllendirilir. TAKTİK: 'how reward creation' sorusunda münhasır hakkı ara. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'risks seeing rivals copy' sorununun tersidir (patent bunu ENGELLER). Şık 3 'grants...sole right' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'sole right' ile çelişir (paylaşmaz). Parantez (which others may not use for years) süstür.
Rowing regattas turned quiet river towns into lively summer destinations.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-071
According to the paragraph, why can a gap between families widen without any fresh effort?

Wealth does not always end quietly with the life that first earned [it].
{Because} riches passed down to children can pile advantage upon advantage across the generations, a gap between families can widen without any fresh [effort].
{So} a fortune inherited rather than earned (which no work of the heir ever created) can quietly shape a whole society's ladder of opportunity.

Because inherited riches pile advantage upon advantage across the generations
Because wealth always ends with the life that first earned it
Because every heir must earn the whole fortune anew
Because inheritance divides all wealth out equally

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — devredilen servet kuşaklar boyu avantaj üstüne avantaj yığar; aradaki uçurum çaba olmadan açılır. TAKTİK: 'widen without effort' sorusunda mirasın biriktirici etkisini ara. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'does not always end with the life' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'inherited rather than earned' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'gap widen' ile çelişir (eşit paylaşmaz). Parantez (which no work of the heir created) süstür.
Language cafes help newcomers practise everyday conversation over cheap coffee.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-072
According to the paragraph, why was the old marketplace far more than a mere place of trade?

The old marketplace sold far more than just fruit and [cloth].
{Because} people of every rank met there to haggle, to gossip, and to hear the latest news, the market became a town's beating social [heart].
{So} to close the market (which quietly bound a whole community together) was to still not only its trade but much of its shared daily life.

Because people of every rank met there to haggle, gossip, and hear the news
Because it sold nothing at all beyond fruit and cloth
Because almost no one ever gathered there in person
Because it worked to keep the community firmly apart

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — her sınıftan insan orada pazarlık eder, dedikodu yapar, haber alırdı; pazar kentin toplumsal kalbiydi. TAKTİK: 'more than trade' sorusunda toplumsal işlevi ara. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'more than fruit and cloth' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'people of every rank met' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'bound a community together' ile çelişir. Parantez (which bound a community together) süstür.
Volunteer fire brigades protected small towns long before professional crews existed.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-073
According to the paragraph, how does charity differ from justice?

A generous gift can ease real suffering, and yet it is not the same thing as [justice].
{Because} charity depends on the goodwill of the giver while a right is owed to all as a matter of law, the two rest on very different [ground].
{So} a hungry family fed by kindness alone (which may simply not come tomorrow) is left far more fragile than one protected by a settled legal claim.

Charity depends on the giver's goodwill, while a right is owed to all by law
Charity is owed to all by law, while justice depends on goodwill
Both of them rest on exactly the same ground
Charity is always far more reliable than a legal right

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi ikisini karşıtlar — hayırseverlik verenin iyi niyetine bağlıdır, hak ise yasayla herkese borçludur. TAKTİK: iki kavramı doğru eşleştir; tanımları çaprazlayan şıkkı ele. Şık 2 tam bu çaprazlamadır. Şık 3 'very different ground' ile çelişir. Şık 4 {So}'daki 'fed by kindness...more fragile' ile çelişir (hak daha güvenilir). Parantez (which may not come tomorrow) süstür.
Canal networks moved coal cheaply between mines and growing cities.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-074
According to the paragraph, why has the power to publish spread to the many?

Once, sharing an idea with the whole world meant owning a printing press or a broadcast [station].
{Because} the internet lets almost anyone with a cheap device reach a vast audience at nearly no cost, the power to publish has spread out to the [many].
{However}, the same open channel that carries real knowledge (which no gatekeeper now filters) also floods us with rumour and empty noise.

Because the internet lets almost anyone reach a vast audience at little cost
Because publishing still demands a press or a broadcast station
Because a careful gatekeeper now filters every message
Because reaching any audience still costs a very great deal

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — internet, ucuz bir cihazı olan hemen herkesin çok geniş kitleye neredeyse bedava ulaşmasını sağlar. TAKTİK: 'why spread to many' sorusunda maliyet/erişim engelinin kalkmasını ara. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki eski, pahalı durumdur (internetin aştığı). Şık 4 'at nearly no cost' ile çelişir. Şık 3 parantezdeki 'no gatekeeper now filters' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Calligraphy classes are enjoying a quiet revival among young city students.
PARA-SOSYAL-70-85-075
According to the paragraph, why does a free public library open learning to the whole community?

A public library hands the very same rich shelves to rich and poor [alike].
{Because} knowledge locked away behind a high price would reach only those who could afford to pay, a free library throws learning open to the whole [community].
{So} a child of no means can read the very same books as the wealthy (which levels one small corner of the world), simply by walking through the door.

Because knowledge behind a high price would reach only those who could pay
Because the library charges the poor far more than the rich
Because it keeps knowledge locked away behind a price
Because only the wealthy are ever allowed to walk in

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — ücretle kilitlenmiş bilgi yalnızca ödeyebilene ulaşırdı; ücretsiz kütüphane öğrenmeyi herkese açar. TAKTİK: 'why open to all' sorusunda ücret engelinin kaldırılmasını ara. Şık 2 'same shelves to rich and poor alike' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'free library' ile çelişir (kilitlemez, açar). Şık 4 'child of no means can read' ile çelişir. Parantez (which levels one small corner...) süstür.
Seed banks preserve rare crop varieties for future generations of farmers.

name: Hızlı Okuma YDS/YDT (70-85)
words: According to the paragraph, why do we put off a hard task even when we know it must be done?

We often put off a hard task even when we know it truly must be [done].
{Because} the mind grabs at the quick relief of avoiding discomfort right now and leaves the cost for later, a looming deadline can still be [ignored].
{However}, the job we keep postponing (which rarely shrinks while we wait) usually grows more daunting with every passing day.

Because the mind grabs the quick relief of avoiding discomfort now
Because the task quietly shrinks while we keep waiting
Because the deadline soon stops looming over us
Because postponing the job actually makes it easier

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi ertelemenin nedenini verir — zihin şimdiki rahatsızlıktan kaçmanın anlık rahatlığına sarılır, bedeli sonraya bırakır. TAKTİK: 'put off' (ertelemek) mantığında anlık kaçış güdüsünü ara. Şık 2 parantezdeki 'rarely shrinks while we wait' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'looming deadline' ile çelişir. Şık 4 {However}'daki 'grows more daunting' ile çelişir.
Coral reefs shelter a quarter of all known marine species worldwide.
According to the paragraph, why can others read us more truly than we intend?

Much of what we say is somehow spoken without a single [word].
{Because} a slumped posture or a wandering gaze can give away feelings the mouth is trying to [hide], others often read us more truly than we ever intend.
{So} a skilled interviewer picks up on these silent signals (which most people leak quite unaware), learning more from how we sit than from what we claim.

Because posture and gaze give away feelings the mouth tries to hide
Because we say absolutely everything in clear, plain words
Because body language in truth always tells a lie
Because interviewers simply ignore all silent signals

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — çökük duruş ya da kaçan bakış, ağzın gizlemeye çalıştığı duyguları ele verir. TAKTİK: beden dili sözden bağımsız 'sızdırır'; niyetimizin ötesini gösterir. Şık 2 'without a single word' ile çelişir. Şık 3 aşırı genelleme ('always lies'). Şık 4 {So}'daki 'interviewer picks up on these signals' ile çelişir. Parantez (which most people leak unaware) süstür.
Glaciers store most of the planet's fresh water in frozen form.
According to the paragraph, why does much of our day run on autopilot?

A habit, once firmly set, can run along almost without our [notice].
{Because} the brain turns a repeated action into an automatic routine in order to save effort, we carry out much of our day on [autopilot].
{However}, this very efficiency that frees the mind (which no longer weighs each single step) also makes a bad habit stubbornly hard to break.

Because the brain turns repeated actions into automatic routines to save effort
Because we carefully weigh each single step we take
Because habits are in fact very easy to break
Because the brain closely notices every action

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi nedeni verir — beyin, çabayı azaltmak için tekrarlanan eylemi otomatik rutine çevirir. TAKTİK: 'autopilot' otomatikleşmedir; bilinçli tartma azalır.
