Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi kutup ışıklarını verir — Güneş'ten gelen yüklü parçacıklar manyetik alanla kutuplara yönlendirilir, havaya çarpıp ışıtır. TAKTİK: 'why aurora' sorusunda parçacık+manyetik alan+çarpışmayı ara. Şık 2 metinde olmayan (yansıma değil). Şık 3 'charged particles...make it glow' ile çelişir. Şık 4 yön hatası (kutba yönlendirilir, itilmez). Parantez (which follows the Sun's storms) süstür.
A caterpillar dissolves almost entirely before rebuilding itself into a winged butterfly.
PARA-FEN-85+-050
According to the paragraph, why does a freely swinging pendulum's path appear to rotate across the floor over hours?

A great pendulum swinging quite freely seems, over the slow passing hours, to gradually change its whole [direction].
{Because} the pendulum stubbornly keeps its own swinging plane fixed in space while the vast Earth quietly turns beneath it, its path only appears to rotate across the [floor].
{So} this stately, silent drift (which needs no pushing force at all to explain it) was the very first plain proof, seen with our own eyes, that the Earth truly [spins].

Because the pendulum keeps its own swinging plane fixed while the Earth turns beneath it
Because some hidden force keeps quietly pushing the pendulum off to one side
Because the Earth itself stays perfectly still and fixed beneath the pendulum
Because the pendulum actively changes its own plane of swing over time

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi Foucault sarkacını verir — sarkaç salınım düzlemini uzayda sabit tutar, Dünya altında döner; yol dönüyormuş gibi görünür. TAKTİK: 'why path rotates' sorusunda sabit düzlem + dönen Dünya'yı ara. Şık 2 parantezdeki 'needs no push to explain' ile çelişir. Şık 3 metnin tezine ('Earth truly spins') zıt. Şık 4 'keeps its plane fixed' ile çelişir (kendi düzlemini değiştirmez). Parantez süstür.
Green plants release the oxygen that nearly every animal needs to breathe.

name: Hızlı Okuma YÖKDİL-Sosyal (85+)
words: PARA-SOSYAL-85+-001
According to the paragraph, why does obedience to the state become a bargain rather than mere submission?

Why should any free person ever bow down to the sheer rule of a [state]?
{Because} thinkers imagined that individuals trade away a little of their wild natural liberty in return for the safety and order only a shared authority can [provide], obedience becomes a bargain rather than blind submission.
{However}, this social contract is a useful fiction, not a signed [deed] (which no living person ever actually put a name to), binding us though we never once agreed.

Because individuals trade away a little wild liberty in return for safety and order
Because every single citizen once signed an actual, dated contract
Because the shared authority in fact provides nothing at all in return
Because obedience really is pure blind submission, with no bargain in it

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi toplum sözleşmesini verir — bireyler bir miktar özgürlüğü, ancak ortak otoritenin sağlayabileceği güvenlik ve düzenle takas eder. TAKTİK: 'why bargain' sorusunda takas fikrini (özgürlük ↔ güvenlik) ara. Şık 2 parantezdeki 'not a signed deed...no one signed' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'only a shared authority can provide' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'a bargain rather than submission' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Rapid urbanization has reshaped family structures across much of the developing world.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-002
According to the paragraph, how can the pursuit of pure self-interest still serve the common good?

A baker rises well before dawn not to feed the whole town but to feed his own [family].
{Because} each trader, chasing only his private gain, must nonetheless offer others exactly what they want at a price they are willing to pay, the pursuit of self-interest can quietly serve the common [good].
{However}, this hidden hand can also fail badly (which unchecked greed soon reveals), whenever private profit and public welfare pull sharply [apart].

Because each trader chasing private gain must still offer others what they want at a price they will pay
Because the traders in truth act only out of pure and selfless charity
Because private profit and public welfare can never once come into conflict
Because the baker actually works in order to feed the whole town

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi görünmez eli verir — kendi çıkarını kovalayan tüccar bile, başkalarına istediklerini uygun fiyata sunmak zorundadır; böylece kamu yararına hizmet eder. TAKTİK: bencillik + rekabet baskısı → ortak fayda. Şık 2 'chasing only his private gain' ile çelişir (hayır değil). Şık 3 {However}'daki 'private profit and public welfare pull apart' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'not to feed the town but his family' ile çelişir. Parantez (which unchecked greed reveals) süstür.
Public museums preserve cultural heritage for generations who cannot yet appreciate it.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-003
According to the paragraph, why should a lawyer who types faster than any clerk still leave the typing to others?

Even a whole nation that is better at making absolutely everything still gains by [trading].
{Because} its time is always best spent on whatever it happens to make most efficiently, leaving others to supply the rest, both sides can end up genuinely richer than [alone].
{So} a brilliant lawyer who also types faster than any clerk she could hire (which seems at first to argue against hiring one) should still leave all the typing to [others].

Because her time is best spent on whatever she does most efficiently, leaving others to supply the rest
Because she is, after all, actually worse at typing than the clerk would be
Because trading in this way always leaves both of the sides poorer than before
Because she really ought to do everything she is best at entirely herself

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi karşılaştırmalı üstünlüğü verir — zaman en verimli işe ayrılmalı, gerisi başkalarına bırakılmalı; iki taraf da zenginleşir. TAKTİK: mutlak değil, GÖRECELİ üstünlük; fırsat maliyeti belirler. Şık 2 parantezdeki 'types faster than any clerk' ile çelişir (aslında daha hızlı). Şık 3 'both sides richer' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'leave the typing to others' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Universal literacy campaigns dramatically expanded access to schooling in rural regions.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-004
According to the paragraph, why do progress and loss so often arrive together?

Almost every great new industry rises directly upon the [ruins] of an older one it replaces.
{Because} a genuinely better way of doing things must sweep away the very firms and jobs built up around the old way, progress and loss tend to arrive together, hand in [hand].
{However}, this same churning that enriches a whole society over the long run (which the displaced themselves rarely feel as any progress) can utterly devastate those whose hard-won skills it renders [obsolete].

Because a better way of doing things must sweep away the firms and jobs built around the old way
Because genuine progress, in the end, never destroys anything at all
Because each brand-new industry in fact rises up out of nothing whatever
Because the displaced workers always feel the change as clear progress

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi yaratıcı yıkımı verir — daha iyi yöntem, eskinin firmalarını ve işlerini süpürmek zorundadır; ilerleme ve kayıp birlikte gelir. TAKTİK: 'why together' sorusunda yeninin eskiyi yıkmasını ara. Şık 2 'must sweep away' ile çelişir (yıkar). Şık 3 'rises upon the ruins of an older one' ile çelişir. Şık 4 parantezdeki 'rarely feel as progress' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Voter turnout among young citizens has declined steadily in many democracies.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-005
According to the paragraph, why are both suspects lured into confessing against each other?

Two suspects, deliberately held apart in separate cells, each face a tempting chance to [betray] the other.
{Because} whatever the other one chooses to do, betraying always looks the safer bet for oneself, both are lured into confessing and so both end up far [worse].
{So} the deep tragedy is that cold reason drives each of them toward a choice (which mutual trust alone could easily have avoided) that leaves them both worse off than silence ever [would].

Because whatever the other does, betraying always looks like the safer bet for oneself
Because simply staying silent clearly looks like the safer bet for each of them
Because the two suspects completely and fully trust one another
Because confessing, as it happens, always leaves them both far better off

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi mahkûm ikilemini verir — diğeri ne yaparsa yapsın, ihanet bireysel olarak daha güvenli görünür; ikisi de itiraf eder ve kaybeder. TAKTİK: baskın strateji ihanettir; bireysel akıl ortak kötü sonuca sürükler. Şık 2 'betraying looks the safer bet' ile çelişir. Şık 3 parantezdeki 'mutual trust could have avoided' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'both end up worse' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Ancient trade routes carried languages and religions as well as merchandise.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-006
According to the paragraph, why can a whole nation saving all at once actually shrink the economy?

In genuinely hard times, each careful household quite wisely tightens its own [belt].
{Because} the very spending that one family cuts back is the exact income that another family earns, a whole nation trying to save all at once can shrink the very economy they had hoped to [protect].
{So} what is plainly prudent for one household alone (which no single saver can ever quite see) can badly deepen the slump when absolutely everyone does it at [once].

Because the spending one family cuts is the very income that another family earns
Because a nation saving all at once always grows the whole economy
Because one family's saving in truth has no effect at all on another
Because cutting back on spending actually raises everyone's income

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi tutumluluk paradoksunu verir — bir ailenin kestiği harcama başka ailenin gelirdir; herkes birden tasarruf edince ekonomi küçülür. TAKTİK: bireysel akıllıca, toplu felaket (bileşim yanılgısı). Şık 2 'shrink the economy' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'one family's spending is another's income' ile çelişir. Şık 4 yön hatası (kesinti geliri düşürür). Parantez (which no single saver can see) süstür.
Minimum wage laws remain fiercely debated among economists and policymakers alike.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-007
According to the paragraph, why does the factory worker grow estranged from the very thing he makes?

A craftsman of old once saw his whole self reflected in the fine chair he had [built].
{Because} the modern factory splits its work into ever tinier fragments, so that a single labourer may spend a whole life fixing just one bolt without ever once seeing the finished [whole], the worker slowly grows estranged from what he makes.
{However}, this alienation is not merely dull and tiring (which better pay alone might ease) but a far deeper loss of all meaning in the [work].

Because the factory splits work into tiny fragments, so he fixes one bolt without ever seeing the whole
Because he plainly sees his whole self reflected in the finished chair
Because simply offering him better pay removes every trace of estrangement
Because he in fact builds the entire finished product all by himself

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi yabancılaşmayı verir — fabrika işi minik parçalara böler; işçi bütünü görmeden tek cıvatayla ömür geçirir, ürüne yabancılaşır. TAKTİK: 'why estranged' sorusunda parçalanmış emeği ara. Şık 2 zanaatkârın (eski) durumudur, fabrika işçisinin değil. Şık 3 {However}'daki 'not merely dull (which better pay might ease)' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'fixing one bolt' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Archaeologists rely on pottery fragments to date early human settlements.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-008
According to the paragraph, why does a bureaucracy trade human warmth for cold consistency?

The very rules that make a huge organisation fair can also render it strangely [soulless].
{Because} treating each and every case by the exact same rigid procedure firmly keeps power from ever playing favourites, bureaucracy knowingly trades warmth for cold, even-handed [consistency].
{However}, the same machinery that guards us all against pure whim (which no mere clerk may ever bend for a friend) can also grind the living individual down into a mere [file].

Because treating every case by the same rigid procedure keeps power from playing favourites
Because it freely lets its clerks bend all the rules for their own friends
Because rigid, identical procedure is exactly what makes an organisation unfair
Because, in the end, it grinds down nobody at all into anything

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi demir kafesi verir — her vakaya aynı katı prosedürü uygulamak, gücün kayırma yapmasını önler; bürokrasi sıcaklığı tutarlılıkla takas eder. TAKTİK: tarafsızlık bedeli = soğukluk. Şık 2 parantezdeki 'no clerk may bend for a friend' ile çelişir. Şık 3 ilk cümledeki 'make an organisation fair' ile çelişir. Şık 4 {However}'daki 'grind the individual down into a file' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Regional dialects fade quickly wherever national broadcasting reaches every household.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-009
According to the paragraph, why are goods like a lighthouse chronically under-supplied by the market?

A lighthouse faithfully guides every passing ship, whether or not that ship's owner ever [pays].
{Because} no one at all can be shut out of a benefit that helps everyone alike, each person is sorely tempted to let all the others foot the bill and simply enjoy it for [free], such goods are chronically under-supplied.
{So} the state very often steps in to fund what all enjoy but none will willingly pay for (a wide gap the free market simply leaves open), from clean air to the common [defence].

Because no one can be shut out, so each is tempted to let others pay and enjoy it for free
Because every single person eagerly pays their own fair share of the cost
Because a lighthouse in fact helps only those few ships whose owners pay
Because the free market always supplies such shared goods completely

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi bedavacılık sorununu verir — kimse dışlanamadığı için herkes başkasının ödemesini bekler; bu yüzden kamu malı yetersiz üretilir. TAKTİK: dışlanamazlık → bedava binme → az arz. Şık 2 'tempted to let others foot the bill' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'whether or not the owner pays' ile çelişir (herkese fayda). Şık 4 'chronically under-supplied' ve {So} devlet müdahalesiyle çelişir. Parantez (a gap the market leaves open) süstür.
Medieval guilds trained apprentices through long years of supervised craftsmanship.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-010
According to the paragraph, why was any rise in a people's wealth soon swallowed for most of history?

For almost the whole of human history, any real rise in a people's wealth was very soon [swallowed].
{Because} more food on the table simply meant more surviving children, whose many extra mouths then dragged living standards right back down to bare [subsistence], the hard-won progress of one generation vanished in the next.
{However}, the industrial age at long last broke this ancient trap (which had firmly bound every single society before it), once economic growth finally began to outrun the [population].

Because more food meant more surviving children, whose extra mouths dragged standards back to subsistence
Because a people's real wealth in fact never rose at all before industry came
Because steadily fewer children happened to be born as the wealth slowly rose
Because economic growth had always easily outrun the growing population

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi Malthus tuzağını verir — daha çok yiyecek daha çok hayatta kalan çocuk demekti; fazla ağızlar yaşam düzeyini geçim sınırına geri çekerdi. TAKTİK: kazanç nüfus artışıyla yutulur. Şık 2 'any rise...was soon swallowed' ile çelişir (yükseldi ama yutuldu). Şık 3 yön hatası (çocuk artar, azalmaz). Şık 4 {However}'daki 'industrial age broke this trap' ile çelişir (öncesi outrun edemezdi). Parantez süstür.
Women's suffrage movements gained decisive momentum in the early twentieth century.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-011
According to the paragraph, why does a society rich in trust spare itself a vast cost?

An economy truly runs not only upon money but upon a great deal of unseen [trust].
{Because} deals close far faster and much more cheaply wherever people can simply expect one another to keep their given word, a society rich in trust spares itself the vast cost of guarding every single [bargain].
{So} where such trust runs thin (which endless locks, contracts, and lawyers must then be paid to replace), even the simplest exchanges grow slow and [dear].

Because deals close faster and cheaper where people expect one another to keep their word
Because a deep supply of trust in fact makes every deal slower and dearer
Because locks, contracts, and lawyers can perfectly replace trust at no cost
Because an economy in truth runs upon nothing whatsoever but hard money

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi sosyal sermayeyi verir — insanlar sözünü tutacak diye beklenen yerde anlaşmalar hızlı ve ucuz kapanır; güven, her pazarlığı koruma masrafından kurtarır. TAKTİK: güven = işlem maliyetini düşüren görünmez yağ. Şık 2 yön hatası (hızlı ve ucuz, yavaş değil). Şık 3 {So}'daki 'must be paid to replace' ile çelişir (bedava değil). Şık 4 'not only upon money but upon trust' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
National censuses reveal striking shifts in household composition over recent decades.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-012
According to the paragraph, why can judging a foreign custom by another culture's yardstick badly mislead us?

A custom that strikes us as plainly barbaric abroad may be entirely ordinary and unremarkable at [home].
{Because} each single practice grows organically out of a whole history and a particular setting all its very own, judging it coldly by some other culture's yardstick can badly [mislead].
{However}, pushing this same sensible idea much too far (which would end up excusing any cruelty at all as mere local custom) can dissolve the very ground on which we rightly condemn a real [wrong].

Because each practice grows out of a whole history and a particular setting all its own
Because every culture on earth in fact shares one single common yardstick
Because customs, in the end, have no real history lying behind them at all
Because any given custom means exactly the same thing absolutely everywhere

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi kültürel göreceliliği verir — her uygulama kendi tarihinden ve bağlamından doğar; başka kültürün ölçütüyle yargılamak yanıltır. TAKTİK: bağlam olmadan yargı yanlış olur. Şık 2 'another culture's yardstick' ile çelişir (ortak ölçüt yok). Şık 3 'grows out of a whole history' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'ordinary at home, barbaric abroad' ile çelişir. Parantez (which would excuse any cruelty) süstür.
Early modern monarchs financed costly wars through increasingly elaborate taxation systems.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-013
According to the paragraph, why does the mere possibility of surveillance do the watching for the guard?

A single guard who merely might be watching from a high central tower needs, in truth, never actually [look].
{Because} prisoners who can never once tell exactly when they are being seen slowly come to behave as though they always [are], the bare possibility of surveillance quietly does all the watching for him.
{So} a lone camera on a busy street corner (which may not even be switched on) can steer a whole crowd's conduct just as surely as a hundred posted [officers].

Because prisoners who cannot tell when they are seen come to behave as though they always are
Because the single guard must, in the end, always actually be looking out
Because the prisoners simply ignore altogether whether they are being watched
Because a street camera can only ever work when it is actually switched on

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi panoptikonu verir — ne zaman görüldüğünü bilemeyen mahkûmlar, hep görülüyormuş gibi davranır; gözetim olasılığı gözetimin işini yapar. TAKTİK: belirsizlik → sürekli öz-denetim. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'needs never actually look' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'behave as though they always are' ile çelişir. Şık 4 parantezdeki 'may not even be switched on' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Aging populations place mounting pressure on public pension systems worldwide.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-014
According to the paragraph, why can insurance against a loss quietly make that very loss more likely?

Insurance taken out against a loss can, oddly, make that very loss more [likely].
{Because} a driver who knows the insurer will simply pay for any dent may come to park with far less [care], being shielded from a risk can quietly tempt us into running it.
{So} a bank quite certain it will be rescued if it ever fails (which its own recklessness then invites) may gamble far more wildly than one left to face its own [ruin].

Because being shielded from a risk can quietly tempt us into running it
Because insurance, as a rule, always makes people much more careful
Because a driver who is fully shielded parks with far greater care
Because simply facing one's own ruin is what invites recklessness

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi ahlaki tehlikeyi verir — riskten korunmak, o riski göze almaya teşvik eder; sigortalı sürücü daha dikkatsiz olur. TAKTİK: koruma → dikkatsizlik. Şık 2 yön hatası (daha dikkatli değil, daha az). Şık 3 'with far less care' ile çelişir. Şık 4 mantık tersi (kendi yıkımıyla yüzleşmek dikkatli kılar, kurtarılma pervasızlaştırır). Parantez (which its recklessness invites) süstür.
Seasonal migration has long shaped labour markets in agricultural economies.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-015
According to the paragraph, why does imagining the rules before knowing your own place force us toward fairness?

To design a genuinely fair society, imagine choosing all its rules before you know your own [place] within it.
{Because} no one who might yet be born poor, sick, or scorned would ever freely choose a world that crushes such people, this single thought forces us hard toward [fairness].
{So} the veil of ignorance (which hides whether you will end up master or servant) quietly turns self-interest itself into a reliable guide toward [justice].

Because no one who might be born poor, sick, or scorned would freely choose a world that crushes such people
Because you already know for certain that you will be the master
Because self-interest, in the end, always leads us away from justice
Because the veil clearly reveals to you your own future place

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi cehalet peçesini verir — yerini bilmeyen kimse yoksulu ezen bir dünyayı seçmez; bu, adaleti zorlar. TAKTİK: kendi konumunu bilmemek → herkesi koruyan kural. Şık 2 parantezdeki 'hides whether master or servant' ile çelişir. Şık 3 {So}'daki 'self-interest into a guide toward justice' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'hides your place' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Eighteenth-century coffeehouses served as lively hubs for political discussion.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-016
According to the paragraph, how can an idea once thought unthinkable become tomorrow's accepted policy?

What a whole society is even willing to discuss shifts slowly and quietly over [time].
{Because} ideas once dismissed as unthinkable can, through sheer repetition and a few daring voices, drift into the range of the merely [debatable], yesterday's wild heresy becomes tomorrow's ordinary policy.
{So} a campaigner who argues hard for the seemingly impossible (which very few will yet accept) may not win at all today, but can still drag the whole window of debate his [way].

Because through repetition and a few daring voices it can drift into the range of the merely debatable
Because what a whole society is willing to discuss in fact never once shifts
Because ideas thought unthinkable simply stay unthinkable forever after
Because the lone campaigner clearly wins the whole argument that very day

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi Overton penceresini verir — tekrar ve cesur sesler, düşünülemez fikri 'tartışılabilir' aralığına kaydırır. TAKTİK: kabul edilebilirlik aralığı kayar. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'shifts slowly over time' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'becomes tomorrow's policy' ile çelişir. Şık 4 {So}'daki 'may not win today' ile çelişir. Parantez (which few will yet accept) süstür.
Remittances from workers abroad sustain millions of households in developing countries.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-017
According to the paragraph, why does an outdated standard stay in place long after its original reason has gone?

The clumsy keyboard right under your fingers was first designed, oddly, to slow hasty typists [down].
{Because} once a standard has been widely learned and endlessly built upon, the sheer cost of everyone switching at once keeps it firmly in place long after its reason has [gone], history can lock a whole society into an inferior choice.
{So} a plainly better layout may well exist (which almost no one will actually adopt), yet the dead weight of all that came before holds the old one [fast].

Because once it is widely learned and built upon, the cost of everyone switching keeps it in place
Because the outdated old standard is, in truth, always the very best one
Because switching over to something new in fact costs nobody anything at all
Because a plainly better layout is always quickly adopted by everyone

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi patika bağımlılığını verir — bir standart yaygın öğrenilip üstüne inşa edilince, herkesin geçiş maliyeti onu ayakta tutar. TAKTİK: geçiş maliyeti → kilitlenme. Şık 2 'inferior choice' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'the cost of everyone switching' ile çelişir. Şık 4 parantezdeki 'almost no one will adopt' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Universities in medieval Europe granted scholars rare freedom to cross borders.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-018
According to the paragraph, why do sheer numbers alone not make a rule just?

A simple vote can come to oppress just as surely as any lone [tyrant].
{Because} a standing majority that always gets exactly its own way can freely trample a minority whose rights it chooses to ignore, sheer numbers alone plainly do not make a rule [just].
{So} a true democracy carefully guards certain rights beyond the reach of any passing vote (which the roused crowd cannot simply override), lest a bare fifty-one percent enslave the other [forty-nine].

Because a majority that always gets its way can trample a minority whose rights it ignores
Because a large majority can, in truth, never once oppress anyone at all
Because a plain vote is, by its very nature, always perfectly and wholly fair
Because it is in fact the minorities who always end up getting their way

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi çoğunluğun tiranlığını verir — her dediğini yaptıran çoğunluk, hakkını yok saydığı azınlığı ezebilir; sayı adaleti garanti etmez. TAKTİK: çoğunluk ≠ adalet. Şık 2 'can oppress as surely as a tyrant' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'do not make a rule just' ile çelişir. Şık 4 azınlığın ezilmesiyle çelişir. Parantez (which the crowd cannot override) süstür.
Modern advertising increasingly targets consumers through detailed analysis of personal data.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-019
According to the paragraph, why does a polluting factory's true damage never show up on the bill?

The strikingly cheap price of a good may quietly leave out its full true [cost].
{Because} a factory that simply dumps its smoke into the shared air pays absolutely nothing for the harm it does, that damage never once shows up on anyone's [bill], and buyer and seller together pass the cost to everyone else.
{So} economists urge that such hidden harms finally be priced in (which the free market on its own entirely ignores), so that the polluter, and not the wider public, at last [pays].

Because the factory that dumps its smoke into the shared air pays nothing for the harm it does

Because street vendors, day labourers, and home workshops pay no tax and appear in no statistic
Because most of the actual work in these countries happens on the official books
Because the informal shadow economy is, in the end, really very small indeed
Because the rigid formal rules already fully include all such casual workers

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi kayıt dışı ekonomiyi verir — seyyar satıcı, gündelikçi ve ev atölyeleri vergi ödemez ve istatistiğe girmez; bu yüzden koca ekonomi göz önünde saklanır. TAKTİK: kayıt dışılık → görünmezlik. Şık 2 'off the official books' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'a vast economy' ile çelişir. Şık 4 parantezdeki 'formal rules shut them out' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Traditional crafts survive today largely through festivals and dedicated apprenticeship schemes.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-040
According to the paragraph, why can a bounty offered on dead cobras end up leading people to breed the snakes?

A reward carefully meant to solve a problem can, perversely, end up quietly [feeding] it instead.
{Because} people in the end follow the actual incentive, and not the good intention lying behind it, a bounty once paid on dead cobras led some clever souls to breed the very snakes for easy [profit].
{So} a well-meant rule can backfire quite spectacularly (which its earnest designers never once foresaw), rewarding the exact mischief it had meant to [end].

Because people in the end follow the actual incentive, and not the good intention behind it
Because people always follow the good intention, and never the raw incentive
Because breeding more cobras genuinely does solve the original problem
Because the designers of a rule foresee its every possible backfire

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi kobra etkisini verir — insanlar niyeti değil teşviği izler; ölü kobra ödülü, para için kobra üretmeye yol açtı. TAKTİK: sapkın teşvik — kural niyetiyle değil ödülüyle işler. Şık 2 tam tersi (teşviği izler, niyeti değil). Şık 3 {So}'daki 'rewarding the very mischief' ile çelişir (çözmez). Şık 4 parantezdeki 'never foresaw' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Commuters in large metropolitan areas lose countless hours to daily congestion.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-041
According to the paragraph, why are some problems solved by mere convention rather than by reason?

It matters remarkably little which side of the road we all drive on, only that we every one of us pick the very [same] side.
{Because} the entire worth of the choice lies wholly in everyone simply agreeing on it, and not in the option itself, some problems are solved by nothing but pure [convention].
{So} once a whole country has settled on the left or on the right (which no reason on its own could ever decide), no lone driver would dare to [differ].

Because the entire worth of the choice lies wholly in everyone agreeing, not in the option itself
Because one side of the road is, in fact, always clearly far better than the other
Because cold reason alone perfectly decides which side we ought to drive on
Because a single lone driver may, in the end, safely choose to differ

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi koordinasyon sorununu verir — seçimin değeri seçeneğin kendisinde değil, herkesin aynı seçimde uzlaşmasındadır. TAKTİK: içerik değil uzlaşma önemli. Şık 2 'matters little which side' ile çelişir. Şık 3 parantezdeki 'no reason alone decides' ile çelişir. Şık 4 {So}'daki 'no lone driver dares to differ' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Wealthy philanthropists founded many of the great nineteenth-century public institutions.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-042
According to the paragraph, why do tiny gaps in skill now yield such vast gaps in pay?

In certain modern markets, the single best performer scoops up very nearly all of the [reward].
{Because} when all the buyers can now reach the very top choice at no extra cost at all, the second-best is left with almost [nothing], the tiniest gaps in skill come to yield enormous gaps in pay.
{So} a singer just a shade better than all her rivals (which once meant very little in a small local hall) may now earn quite literally a thousand times [more].

Because when buyers can all reach the top choice at no extra cost, the second-best is left with almost nothing
Because the second-best performer, in fact, earns very nearly as much as the best
Because a performer's raw skill has, in the end, no real effect on their pay
Because the buyers simply cannot ever reach the single top choice at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi kazanan-hepsini-alır ekonomisini verir — alıcılar en iyiye bedava ulaşabildiğinden ikinci sıradakine neredeyse hiçbir şey kalmaz; küçük yetenek farkı büyük ücret farkı doğurur. TAKTİK: en iyiye kolay erişim → uçurum. Şık 2 'almost nothing' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'vast gaps in pay' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'buyers can all reach the top choice' ile çelişir. Parantez (which once meant little...) süstür.
Night schools gave working adults a second chance at formal education.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-043
According to the paragraph, why were the untouched areas of the returning warplanes in truth the fatal ones?

Engineers early in the war moved to armour their warplanes exactly where the returning ones came back most [riddled] with holes.
{Because} the planes that had been shot in those very same spots had, after all, still managed to make it safely home, the strangely untouched areas were in cold truth the truly [fatal] ones.
{So} the genuinely smart move was to shield instead where the survivors were unscathed (which quietly counted the missing, not the returned), the very places where a single hit brought a plane [down].

Because the planes shot in those spots had not made it home to be counted at all
Because the returning planes had been shot there and yet survived it easily
Because the visible holes always reliably mark out the most dangerous spots
Because it was the missing planes, and not the returned ones, that got counted

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi hayatta kalan yanlılığını verir — o noktalardan vurulan uçaklar eve dönemediği için sayılamaz; dokunulmamış bölgeler asıl ölümcül yerlerdir. TAKTİK: örneklem yalnızca 'dönenlerden' oluşur (eksikler görünmez). Şık 2 yön hatası (dokunulmamış bölge asıl tehlike). Şık 3 tam bu yanlış sezgidir (delik = tehlike sanmak). Şık 4 parantezdeki 'counted the missing, not the returned' düşüncesinin tersini olgu sanır. Parantez süstür.
Ancient coinage spread rapidly once merchants recognized its convenience for exchange.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-044
According to the paragraph, why do both people and nations tend to spend now and let the reckoning wait?

We quite routinely value a small, certain gain right today over a far larger one promised [tomorrow].
{Because} the whole future feels faint, distant, and deeply uncertain beside the sharp and vivid present, both individual people and whole nations tend to spend freely now and simply let the reckoning [wait].
{So} a forest felled all at once for a quick easy profit (which no future voter can ever rise up to protest) may badly impoverish a whole generation not yet even [born].

Because the whole future feels faint, distant, and uncertain beside the sharp and vivid present
Because a far larger gain promised tomorrow, in fact, always wins out over today
Because the present, oddly, feels far more faint and distant than the future does
Because the future voters can, after all, easily rise up and protest the choice

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi kısa vadeciliği (gelecek iskontosu) verir — gelecek, canlı bugünün yanında soluk kaldığından şimdi harcanır, hesap ertelenir. TAKTİK: canlı bugün > soluk gelecek. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'value a small gain today over a larger tomorrow' ile çelişir. Şık 3 yön hatası (gelecek soluk, bugün canlı). Şık 4 parantezdeki 'no future voter can protest' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Refugee resettlement programmes depend heavily on cooperation between neighbouring governments.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-045
According to the paragraph, why does power lie as much in silence as in open speech?

The daily news cannot quite tell us exactly what to think, but it can powerfully tell us what to think [about].
{Because} by quietly choosing which stories to run big and which to bury deep, editors set the very boundaries of the whole public [debate], real power lies as much in careful silence as in open speech.
{So} an issue kept firmly off the front page (which quietly shapes what a whole nation simply ignores) can vanish from all public concern without one word ever being formally [censored].

Because by choosing which stories to run and which to bury, editors set the boundaries of public debate
Because the daily news does, in the end, tell us exactly and precisely what to think
Because the editors, as a rule, run absolutely every story with equal weight
Because an issue must first be formally censored before it can ever vanish

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi gündem belirlemeyi verir — editörler hangi haberin öne çıkıp hangisinin gömüleceğini seçerek tartışmanın sınırlarını çizer; sessizlik de güçtür. TAKTİK: ne gösterileceğini seçmek = gündemi belirlemek. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'cannot tell us what to think' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'which to bury' ile çelişir (eşit değil). Şık 4 {So}'daki 'without a word being censored' ile çelişir. Parantez (which shapes what a nation ignores) süstür.
Grand international exhibitions showcased industrial progress to enormous nineteenth-century crowds.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-046
According to the paragraph, why can a fast-rising country's growth stall well short of true wealth?

A genuinely poor country can grow strikingly fast for a while simply by copying others and by its own cheap [labour].
{Because} those very same easy advantages inevitably fade as its wages steadily rise and the simple catching-up finally runs out, its growth can stall out well short of real [wealth].
{However}, truly breaking through then demands a far harder leap toward genuine invention (which very few nations ever quite manage), moving from making others' designs to boldly creating one's very [own].

Because the advantages of cheap labour and easy catching-up fade as its wages steadily rise
Because a country's cheap labour, in truth, never once loses its early advantage
Because the hard leap to genuine invention is, in fact, the very easiest of all
Because the simple, cheap catching-up phase, as it happens, never runs out at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi orta gelir tuzağını verir — ucuz emek ve taklit avantajı, ücretler artıp yakalama bitince solar; büyüme zenginliğe varmadan durur. TAKTİK: kolay avantajların tükenişi. Şık 2 'those advantages fade' ile çelişir. Şık 3 {However}'daki 'a far harder leap' ile çelişir (kolay değil). Şık 4 'the easy catching-up runs out' ile çelişir. Parantez (which few nations manage) süstür.
Bilingual education helps immigrant children maintain strong ties with their heritage.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-047
According to the paragraph, why may a threat that worsens only by tiny steps never trip the alarm?

A real danger that creeps in slowly enough can escape our notice [entirely].
{Because} we react sharply and at once to a sudden shock but quietly adjust ourselves to a merely gradual one, a threat that worsens only by tiny, patient steps may never once trip the [alarm].
{So} a whole society sliding by slow degrees toward a crisis (which no single passing day ever makes quite plain) can wake far too late to the very change it never chose to [see].

Because we react sharply to a sudden shock but quietly adjust ourselves to a merely gradual one
Because we in fact react most sharply of all to slow and gradual change
Because a slowly creeping danger is, as a rule, always noticed at once
Because one single passing day makes the whole gradual change perfectly plain

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi 'kaynayan kurbağa'yı verir — ani şoka keskin tepki veririz ama kademeli değişime sessizce uyum sağlarız; yavaş tehdit alarmı çaldırmaz. TAKTİK: yavaşlık algıyı köreltir. Şık 2 yön hatası (yavaşa uyum sağlar, keskin tepki vermez). Şık 3 'may never trip the alarm' ile çelişir. Şık 4 parantezdeki 'no single day makes it plain' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Pilgrimage routes across medieval Europe supported inns, markets, and countless towns.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-048
According to the paragraph, why might cold logic conclude that staying home on election day is rational?

A single individual vote almost never actually decides a whole [election].
{Because} the truly tiny chance that any one ballot tips the final result seems far too small to ever justify the real trouble of casting it, cold, narrow logic quietly whispers that simply staying home is [rational].
{However}, if every last person who reasoned exactly so then stayed away (which democracy itself plainly could not long survive), the whole system would quietly [collapse].

Because the tiny chance that one ballot tips the result seems too small to justify the trouble
Because a single individual vote, in fact, almost always decides the whole election
Because the simple act of voting, in truth, costs a person no trouble whatsoever
Because a healthy democracy actually thrives best when all of its people stay home

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi oy paradoksunu verir — tek oyun sonucu çevirme ihtimali, oy verme zahmetini haklı çıkaramayacak kadar küçük görünür; dar mantık evde kalmayı 'akılcı' der. TAKTİK: bireysel maliyet-fayda tek oyu değersiz gösterir. Şık 2 'almost never decides' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'the trouble of casting it' ile çelişir. Şık 4 {However}'daki 'democracy could not survive' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Cooperative housing movements gave many urban workers their first secure homes.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-049
According to the paragraph, why is much of our social world real only because we all treat it as real?

A crisp banknote is really just a scrap of printed paper worth only whatever we all quietly agree it [is].
{Because} money, borders, and grand titles hold no power at all in raw nature but only ever in our shared belief, much of our whole social world is real precisely because we choose to treat it as [real].
{So} a mere line drawn across a map (which the bare land itself never once marks) can genuinely start a war, though not a single fence stands upon the actual [ground].

Because money, borders, and titles hold no power in raw nature but only in our shared belief
Because a crisp banknote is, in the end, genuinely valuable all in itself
Because borders are, in fact, plainly and physically marked out by the land itself
Because our shared belief has, in truth, no real power over the social world at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi gerçekliğin toplumsal inşasını verir — para, sınır ve unvanlar doğada değil ortak inançta güç taşır; dünyamızın çoğu, öyle davrandığımız için gerçektir. TAKTİK: kurumsal olgular kolektif kabulle var olur. Şık 2 'worth only what we agree it is' ile çelişir. Şık 3 parantezdeki 'the land never marks it' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'only in shared belief' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Oral historians record elderly villagers before their memories vanish forever.
PARA-SOSYAL-85+-050
According to the paragraph, why does a threat that is everyone's business so often become nobody's?

A slow-moving disaster that quietly harms absolutely everyone at once may, in the end, be tackled by [none].
{Because} each single person keeps waiting for someone else to step up and bear the heavy cost of acting first, a pressing threat that is truly everyone's business steadily becomes precisely [nobody's].
{So} a vast shared danger such as a warming climate (which no single hand alone could ever hope to halt) can drift on wholly unaddressed while each one quietly waits for the [others].

Because each single person keeps waiting for someone else to bear the cost of acting first
Because absolutely everyone, in fact, rushes at once to be the first to act
Because a slow-moving disaster of this kind, in truth, harms almost no one at all
Because one single determined hand can, after all, easily halt the whole thing

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi kolektif eylemsizliği verir — herkes ilk maliyeti başkasının üstlenmesini beklediğinden, herkesin işi kimsenin işi olmaktan çıkar. TAKTİK: sorumluluğun dağılması → toplu atalet. Şık 2 tam tersi (kimse ilk davranmak istemez). Şık 3 'harms everyone at once' ile çelişir. Şık 4 parantezdeki 'no single hand can halt' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
School meal programmes noticeably raise attendance among children from disadvantaged families.

name: Hızlı Okuma YDS/YDT (85+)
words: PARA-YDS-85+-001
According to the paragraph, why might a thing's identity lie in its pattern rather than in its matter?

If every single plank of an old ship is replaced one slow plank at a time, is it truly still the same [ship]?
{Because} not one splinter of the original timber remains, and yet the whole form and function persist quite unbroken, identity may in the end lie in the pattern rather than in the raw [matter].
{So} a human body that swaps out every one of its atoms across the years (which no cell of childhood ever survives) may still be, in every way that counts, the very same [person].

Because not one splinter of the original timber remains, yet the form and function persist unbroken
Because it is precisely the original timber that always stays the very same
Because the pattern steadily changes while only the matter stays the same
Because not a single cell of our childhood survives the passing years

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi Theseus'un gemisini verir — özgün malzeme kalmasa da biçim ve işlev sürdüğünden kimlik desende olabilir. TAKTİK: kimlik = madde değil örüntü. Şık 2 'not one splinter remains' ile çelişir. Şık 3 yön hatası (desen sürer, madde değişir). Şık 4 doğru bir olgu ama 'why pattern' sorusunu yanıtlamaz (analojinin ayrıntısı). Parantez (which no cell survives) süstür.
Ocean temperatures rise gradually and bleach coral reefs across tropical waters.
PARA-YDS-85+-002
According to the paragraph, why do some argue that our very sense of choosing is only an illusion?

If each and every thought springs directly from a long chain of prior [causes], can any of our choices ever be truly free?
{Because} the very same physical laws that steer a falling stone also fire the neurons lying behind a human decision, some thinkers argue that our whole sense of freely choosing is a mere [illusion].
{However}, the plain fact that this feeling remains so utterly unshakeable (which no clever argument ever quite dispels) has kept the ancient debate fiercely alive for [centuries].

Because the same physical laws that steer a falling stone also fire the neurons behind a decision
Because our choices, in truth, spring from no prior causes whatsoever
Because the feeling of freely choosing is, in fact, very easily dispelled
Because the whole debate was, in the end, quietly settled centuries ago

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi determinizm savını verir — taşı düşüren yasalar kararın nöronlarını da ateşler; öyleyse seçim yanılsama olabilir. TAKTİK: aynı fizik yasası → özgürlük kuşkusu. Şık 2 ilk cümledeki 'chain of prior causes' ile çelişir. Şık 3 parantezdeki 'no argument dispels' ile çelişir. Şık 4 {However}'daki 'kept the debate alive' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
Central banks adjust interest rates to keep inflation within a stable range.
PARA-YDS-85+-003
According to the paragraph, why does the deepest puzzle of the mind still stubbornly endure?

We can now map out very nearly every single neuron that fires the moment you see the colour [red], and yet still not know at all why it feels like anything whatsoever.
{Because} explaining the sheer physical machinery of the brain leaves entirely untouched the raw inner experience it somehow [produces], the very deepest puzzle of the mind quietly endures.
{So} even a perfect and complete account of all the wiring (which tells us fully how but never once why) may still miss the whole mystery of the [felt].

Because explaining the physical machinery of the brain leaves untouched the raw inner experience it produces
Because we cannot, in fact, map out even a single one of the neurons
Because the brain's wiring already fully and completely explains the felt experience
Because the raw inner experience has, in truth, no real puzzle to it at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi bilincin zor problemini verir — beynin mekaniğini açıklamak, onun ürettiği ham iç deneyimi açıklamaz; gizem sürer. TAKTİK: 'how' açıklanır ama 'why it feels' açıklanmaz. Şık 2 'we can map nearly every neuron' ile çelişir. Şık 3 parantezdeki 'never once why' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'the deepest puzzle endures' ile çelişir. Parantez (which tells us how but not why) süstür.
Bilingual children often develop stronger skills in switching between mental tasks.
PARA-YDS-85+-004
According to the paragraph, how can the words a language gives us quietly shape the very thoughts we can think?

The particular words that a language hands us may quietly go on to shape the very thoughts that we are able to [think].
{Because} a tongue rich with many separate words for a single colour or a subtle feeling lets its own speakers notice fine distinctions that others may entirely [miss], language turns out to be not just a plain tool but a lens.
{However}, just how far it truly bounds our deepest thinking (which fierce ongoing study still hotly contests) remains very far indeed from [settled].

Because a tongue rich with many words for something lets its speakers notice distinctions others may miss
Because language is, in the end, only ever a plain and perfectly neutral tool
Because the whole question has, in fact, already been fully and finally settled
Because the words we use never once affect what we are able to notice

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi dilsel göreceliliği verir — bir şey için çok sözcüğü olan dil, konuşanına başkalarının kaçırdığı ayrımları fark ettirir. TAKTİK: dil = araç değil, mercek. Şık 2 'not just a tool but a lens' ile çelişir. Şık 3 {However}'daki 'far from settled' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'notice distinctions others may miss' ile çelişir. Parantez (which study still contests) süstür.
Melting glaciers steadily raise sea levels along low-lying coastal regions.
PARA-YDS-85+-005
According to the paragraph, why can one single canvas hold as many meanings as there are eyes to see it?

The very moment a painter finally lays down her brush, the whole meaning of the finished work slips quietly from her own [grasp].
{Because} each and every viewer brings a complete lifetime of private memory to whatever it is they see, a single canvas can end up holding as many meanings as there are watching [eyes], the artist's own intent is only ever one voice among many.
{So} a poem read a full century on (which its long-dead author could never have foreseen) may say things she herself never once meant to [say].

Because each and every viewer brings a complete lifetime of private memory to whatever they see
Because the artist's own intent is, in the end, the single and only meaning
Because a canvas can only ever hold one single, fixed, and final meaning
Because the watching viewers bring no memory at all to whatever they see

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi sanatın yorumunu verir — her izleyici esere bir ömürlük belleğini getirir; bir tuval göz sayısı kadar anlam taşır. TAKTİK: anlam izleyiciyle çoğalır. Şık 2 'only one voice among many' ile çelişir. Şık 3 'as many meanings as eyes' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'brings a lifetime of memory' ile çelişir. Parantez (which the author could not foresee) süstür.
Global supply chains connect distant factories to shoppers in a single market.
PARA-YDS-85+-006
According to the paragraph, why does the writer say that morality is not mere counting?

Would you yourself divert a runaway trolley so that it kills only one person and thereby spares [five]?
{Because} our deep gut recoils in horror from physically pushing a man to his death, yet quietly accepts flipping a distant switch that dooms him just the same, the very same arithmetic can somehow feel either right or [wrong], and so morality is plainly not mere counting.
{So} a hard choice that clearly saves the greater number of lives (which cold, pure logic would surely applaud) may still strike us deep down as a [crime].

Because the same arithmetic can somehow feel either right or wrong depending on how the act is done
Because saving the greater number of lives, in fact, always simply feels right to us
Because morality is, in the very end, exactly and precisely the same as counting
Because our deep gut, in truth, never once recoils from any act whatsoever

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi tramvay problemini verir — aynı sayısal sonuç, eylem biçimine göre doğru ya da yanlış hissettirir; ahlak yalnız saymak değildir. TAKTİK: aynı aritmetik, farklı sezgi. Şık 2 'can feel right or wrong' ile çelişir ('always right' yanlış). Şık 3 'not mere counting' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'our gut recoils' ile çelişir. Parantez (which cold logic would applaud) süstür.
Vaccines train the immune system to recognize dangerous invaders before infection.
PARA-YDS-85+-007
According to the paragraph, why does an open society's very openness need a firm limit in order to survive?

A society that chooses to tolerate absolutely everything may, in the end, tolerate its own quiet [end].
{Because} an unlimited tolerance extended even to those wholly bent on crushing tolerance itself can hand them the very freedom that they would gladly [abolish], a genuine openness plainly needs some limit if it is to survive at all.
{So} truly defending an open society (which simply cannot be allowed to permit its own destruction) may sometimes mean flatly refusing to tolerate the deeply [intolerant].

Because unlimited tolerance extended to those bent on crushing it can hand them the freedom they would abolish
Because a genuinely open and tolerant society has, in fact, no real enemies at all
Because an open society truly must be allowed to permit its very own destruction
Because it is the deeply intolerant who, in the end, defend openness the best

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi hoşgörü paradoksunu verir — hoşgörüyü ezmeye kararlı olana bile sınırsız hoşgörü, onlara yok etmek istedikleri özgürlüğü verir; açıklık sınır ister. TAKTİK: sınırsız hoşgörü kendini yok eder. Şık 2 'those bent on crushing tolerance' ile çelişir (düşman var). Şık 3 parantezdeki 'cannot allow its own destruction' ile çelişir. Şık 4 'the intolerant' ile çelişir (savunmaz, tehdit eder). Parantez süstür.
Distant galaxies drift apart as the expanding universe steadily stretches empty space.
PARA-YDS-85+-008
According to the paragraph, why can we never squeeze a moral duty out of a mere observation of fact?

No towering pile of plain facts about how the world simply is can, on its own, ever tell us how it truly [ought] to be.
{Because} a bare description of the world, however utterly complete it may be, contains within it no hidden command at all, we can never squeeze out a genuine duty from a mere neutral [observation].
{So} the plain truth that nature is red in tooth and claw (which only describes the world but never once justifies it) tells us precisely nothing of how we ourselves should [live].

Because a bare description of the world, however complete, contains within it no hidden command
Because a pile of plain facts alone does, in fact, clearly tell us exactly how to live
Because even a bare description of the world does secretly contain a hidden command

{So} a kind enough word offered coolly from above (which comforts the smug giver far more than the given) can quietly wound just where a true fellow-feeling would instead [heal].

Because pity keeps the sufferer at a safe distance while empathy actually shares their heavy burden
Because pity and empathy are, when you look closely, in fact exactly the same thing
Because it is warm empathy, and not cold pity, that looks down upon the sufferer
Because a kind word offered coolly from above always, in the end, heals rather than wounds

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi empati-acıma ayrımını verir — acıma acı çekeni güvenli mesafede tutar, empati yükünü paylaşır; ikisi çok farklı avutur. TAKTİK: acıma yukarıdan, empati yanında. Şık 2 'very different ways' ile çelişir. Şık 3 yön hatası (acıma yukarıdan bakar, empati değil). Şık 4 {So}'daki 'can quietly wound' ile çelişir. Parantez (which comforts the giver more) süstür.
Solar flares can disrupt satellites and knock out power grids on earth.
PARA-YDS-85+-048
According to the paragraph, why can a single well-aimed question teach us more than a ready-made answer?

The very best of teachers may well choose to answer a hard question with yet another sharper [question].
{Because} a truth that we ourselves are gently led to find takes far deeper root within us than one that is simply handed straight to [us], a single good question can teach a great deal more than any ready answer.
{So} a wise mentor who quietly asks 'and just why do you think that?' (which forces the lazy mind to work) builds a deep understanding no mere lecture could ever hope to [instil].

Because a truth we are gently led to find ourselves takes far deeper root than one handed to us
Because a ready-made answer, when simply handed over, in fact takes the very deepest root
Because a well-aimed question, in truth, teaches a person absolutely nothing at all
Because a long formal lecture is what builds the very deepest understanding of all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi Sokratik yöntemi verir — kendimizin bulmaya yöneltildiği hakikat, verilenden daha derine kök salar; iyi soru hazır cevaptan çok öğretir. TAKTİK: kendin keşfetmek > hazır cevap. Şık 2 yön hatası (verilen değil, bulunan kök salar). Şık 3 'can teach a great deal more' ile çelişir. Şık 4 {So}'daki 'no lecture could instil' ile çelişir. Parantez (which forces the mind to work) süstür.
Overfishing has emptied once-teeming waters of their largest predatory fish.
PARA-YDS-85+-049
According to the paragraph, why can simply pausing turn out to be the most productive act of them all?

A good farming field left quietly fallow for one whole season will, in the end, yield a great deal more than one worked without any [rest].
{Because} true rest is not really the mere absence of all work but is in fact a living part of it, letting both the tired ground and the weary mind slowly recover their lost [strength], simply pausing can be the single most productive act of all.
{So} a deep thinker who deliberately steps well away from a stubborn problem for a time (which the exhausted mind only ever tightens) so often returns to find the whole answer quietly waiting in plain [view].

Because rest lets both the tired ground and the weary mind slowly recover their lost strength
Because true rest is, in the very end, really nothing more than the mere absence of all work
Because a tired and exhausted mind is what best loosens and solves a stubborn problem
Because deliberately stepping away from a hard problem, in truth, never once helps at all

Doğru cevap 1: {Because} cümlesi dinlenmenin değerini verir — dinlenme işin yokluğu değil parçasıdır; toprağın ve zihnin gücünü toplamasına izin verir. TAKTİK: mola = üretkenliğin parçası. Şık 2 'not the absence of work but a part of it' ile çelişir. Şık 3 parantezdeki 'the tired mind only tightens' ile çelişir (gevşetmez). Şık 4 {So}'daki 'returns to find the answer' ile çelişir. Parantez süstür.
The sun converts hydrogen into helium, releasing enormous energy every second.
PARA-YDS-85+-050
According to the paragraph, why is honest self-knowledge the very rarest and slowest of all wisdom?

The single hardest thing of all to ever see clearly may well be, in the end, one's own [self].
{Because} we stand far too close to all our own motives, and are far too kind to all our own faults, to ever quite judge them plainly, true self-knowledge is the very rarest and the slowest [wisdom] of all.
{So} a whole life never once turned quietly inward to ask what it is truly even for (which the wise ancients thought scarcely worth the living) may drift right through all its days only half [awake].

Because we stand too close to our own motives, and are too kind to our own faults, to judge them plainly
Because our very own self is, in fact, the single easiest thing of all to see clearly
Because we judge all of our own faults far more harshly than we judge anyone else's
Because the wise ancients thought the examined, inward-turned life scarcely worth living at all
